title.zh: 卷二百六十六 列傳第一百五十四 馬世奇 吳麟徵 周鳳翔 劉理順 汪偉 吳甘來 王章 陳良謨 陳純德 申佳胤 成德 許直 金鉉
title.en: Volume 266 Biographies 154: Ma Shiqi, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Chen Chunde, Shen Jiayin, Cheng De, Xu Zhi, Jin Xuan
title.raw: 卷二百六十六 列傳第一百五十四 馬世奇 吳麟徵 周鳳翔 劉理順 汪偉 吳甘來 王章 陳良謨 陳純德 申佳胤 成德 許直 金鉉 Volume 266 Biographies 154: Ma Shiqi, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Chen Chunde, Shen Jiayin, Cheng De, Xu Zhi, Jin Xuan

sentences.zh: 馬世奇吳麟征周鳳翔劉理順汪偉吳甘來王章陳良謨陳純德申佳允成德許直金鉉

translations.literal: Ma Shiqi, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Chen Chunde, Shen Jiayun, Cheng De, Xu Zhi, and Jin Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiqi, Wu Linzheng, Zhou Fengxiang, Liu Lishun, Wang Wei, Wu Ganlai, Wang Zhang, Chen Liangmo, Chen Chunde, Shen Jiayun, Cheng De, Xu Zhi, and Jin Xuan.

sentences.zh: 馬世奇，字君常，無錫人。

translations.literal: Ma Shiqi, styled Junchang, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiqi, whose courtesy name was Junchang, came from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 祖濂，進士，桂林知府。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lian was a jinshi and served as prefect of Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lian had passed the jinshi examination and held the post of prefect of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 世奇幼穎異，嗜學有文名。

translations.literal: In youth Shiqi was exceptionally bright, devoted to study, and had a literary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Shiqi was unusually quick-witted; he loved learning and was already known for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 登崇禎四年進士，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fourth year of Chongzhen, was made a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign he took his jinshi degree, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝遣詞臣分諭諸藩。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor dispatched literary officials to deliver pronouncements separately to the various princely establishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of his reign the emperor sent literary officials to announce imperial messages to the various princely domains.

sentences.zh: 世奇使山東、湖廣、江西諸王府，所至卻饋遺。

translations.literal: Shiqi was sent to the princely mansions of Shandong, Huguang, and Jiangxi; wherever he went he refused gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was assigned to the princely courts of Shandong, Huguang, and Jiangxi, and at every stop he turned away presents offered to him.

sentences.zh: 還，進左諭德。

translations.literal: Upon his return he was promoted to Left Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When he came back to the capital he was promoted to Left Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 久之還朝，進左庶子。

translations.literal: After a long interval he returned to court and was promoted to Left Sub-Reader.
translations.idiomatic: After a long absence he returned to court and was made Left Sub-Reader.

sentences.zh: 帝數召廷臣問禦寇策。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly summoned court ministers to ask their strategies for repelling the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often called in court officials to hear their plans for dealing with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 世奇言：「闖、獻二賊，除獻易，除闖難。

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "Of the two bandit leaders, Chuang and Xian, eliminating Xian is easy, eliminating Chuang is hard.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Of the two rebel chiefs, Li Zicheng and Zhang Xianzhong, it is easy to destroy Zhang but hard to destroy Li.

sentences.zh: 人心畏獻而附闖，非附闖也，苦兵也。

translations.literal: People's hearts fear Xian but attach to Chuang—not that they truly side with Chuang, but that they suffer under government troops.
translations.idiomatic: The people fear Zhang yet drift toward Li—not because they love Li, but because they are worn down by government armies.

sentences.zh: 今欲收人心，惟敕督撫鎮將嚴束部伍，使兵不虐民，民不苦兵，則亂可弭。」

translations.literal: Now if we wish to win hearts, we need only order governors, grand coordinators, and regional commanders to strictly discipline their troops so that soldiers do not abuse the people and the people are not ground down by the army—then disorder can be quelled.
translations.idiomatic: If we want to win the people back, we must command governors, coordinators, and garrison commanders to keep their men in strict order so troops do not prey on civilians and civilians are not crushed by the military—then the turmoil can be stilled.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，為下詔申飭。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and issued an edict to reinforce discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought well of this advice and issued an edict calling for stricter discipline.

sentences.zh: 時寇警日亟，每召對，諸大臣無能畫一策。

translations.literal: At the time bandit alarms grew daily more urgent; at each imperial audience not one minister could propose a unified plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit alarms grew worse by the day; whenever the emperor summoned his ministers, none could offer a coherent strategy.

sentences.zh: 世奇歸邸，輒太息泣下，曰：「事不可為矣。」

translations.literal: Returning to his residence Shiqi would sigh deeply and weep, saying: "The situation can no longer be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his house Shiqi would sigh and weep, saying, "There is nothing left to be done.

sentences.zh: 十七年三月，城陷。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventeenth year the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the seventeenth year the city fell.

sentences.zh: 世奇方早食，投箸起，問帝安在、東宮二王安在，或言帝已出城，或言崩，或又言東宮二王被執。

translations.literal: Shiqi was at his morning meal; he cast down his chopsticks and rose, asking where the emperor was and where the two princes of the Eastern Palace were. Some said the emperor had already left the city, some said he had died, others said the two princes had been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi was at breakfast when he threw down his chopsticks and stood up, demanding to know where the emperor was and where the two crown princes were. Some said the emperor had fled the city, some that he was dead, others that both princes had been seized.

sentences.zh: 世奇曰：「嗟乎，吾不死安之！」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "Alas—if I do not die, where shall I go?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "Alas—if I do not die, where else can I turn?

sentences.zh: 其仆曰：「如太夫人何？」

translations.literal: His servant said: "What of your lady mother?"
translations.idiomatic: His servant asked, "What about your mother?"

sentences.zh: 世奇曰：「正恐辱太夫人耳。」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "It is precisely because I fear dishonoring Lady Mother."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied, "It is because I fear I would bring shame upon her."

sentences.zh: 將自經，二妾朱、李盛飾前。

translations.literal: As he was about to hang himself, his two concubines Zhu and Li came forward in full dress.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to hang himself, his two concubines Zhu and Li appeared before him in their finest attire.

sentences.zh: 世奇訝曰：「若以我死，將辭我去耶？」

translations.literal: Shiqi said in surprise: "Do you mean to take leave of me because I am about to die?
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said in astonishment, "Are you taking leave of me because I am about to die?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「聞主人盡節，我二人來從死耳。」

translations.literal: They replied: "Hearing that our master will die for his duty, we two have come to follow you in death."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We heard that our master would die for his principles, and we two have come to die with you."

sentences.zh: 世奇曰：「有是哉！」

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "It is truly so!"
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said, "So it is!"

sentences.zh: 二妾並自經，世奇端坐，引帛自力縊乃死。

translations.literal: Both concubines hanged themselves together; Shiqi sat upright and, drawing the silk cord taut with his own strength, strangled himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Both concubines hanged themselves at once; Shiqi sat erect, pulled the cord tight with his own hands, and strangled himself to death.

sentences.zh: 先是，兵部主事成德將死，貽書世奇，以慷慨從容二義質焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cheng De of the Ministry of War, about to die, sent Shiqi a letter asking him to choose between the two principles of dying heroically or dying calmly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Cheng De, a secretary in the Ministry of War, facing death, had written to Shiqi asking whether he would choose a passionate death or a composed one.

sentences.zh: 世奇曰：「勉哉元升。

translations.literal: Shiqi said: "Take heart, Yuansheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi wrote back, "Press on, Yuansheng.

sentences.zh: 吾人見危授命，吾不為其難，誰為其難者！

translations.literal: When we meet danger we offer our lives—if I do not undertake this hard course, who will?
translations.idiomatic: When danger comes, a gentleman gives his life—if I will not do this hard thing, who will?

sentences.zh: 與君攜手黃泉，預訂斯盟，無忘息壤矣。」

translations.literal: Let us join hands in the Yellow Springs; we have made this pact in advance—do not forget it, as one forgets not the soil of Xirang.
translations.idiomatic: Let us join hands in the underworld; we have sealed this pact beforehand—do not forget it, as one does not forget a vow sworn on the soil of Xirang.

sentences.zh: 世奇修頤廣顙，揚眉大耳，砥名行，居館閣有聲，好推獎後進。

translations.literal: Shiqi had a long beard and broad forehead, arched brows and large ears; he polished his reputation and conduct, was esteemed in the Hanlin Academy, and delighted in promoting younger men.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi wore a long beard and had a broad forehead, high brows, and large ears; he cultivated his moral reputation, was respected in the Academy, and liked to encourage younger scholars.

sentences.zh: 為人廉，父死，蘇州推官倪長圩以贖鍰三千助喪。

translations.literal: He was personally incorruptible. When his father died, the investigating censor of Suzhou Ni Changxu offered three thousand taels of commutated fines to assist with the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of integrity. When his father died, Ni Changxu, the investigating censor of Suzhou, offered three thousand taels in commutated fines to help with the funeral expenses.

sentences.zh: 世奇辭曰：「蘇饑，留此可用振。」

translations.literal: Shiqi declined, saying: "Suzhou is suffering famine—keep this; it may be used for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi refused, saying, "Suzhou is in famine—keep this money; it can be used for relief.

sentences.zh: 座主周延儒再相，世奇同郡遠嫌，除服不赴都。

translations.literal: His patron Zhou Yanru again became chief minister; being from the same prefecture Shiqi kept his distance and did not go to the capital when his mourning period ended.
translations.idiomatic: When his patron Zhou Yanru became chief minister again, Shiqi, being from the same district, kept his distance and did not return to the capital after his mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，延儒已賜死，親昵者率避去，世奇經紀其喪。

translations.literal: When he finally returned to court Yanru had already been sentenced to death; intimates for the most part steered clear, but Shiqi arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he returned to court Yanru had already been put to death; most of his close associates kept away, but Shiqi saw to his funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 其好義如此。

translations.literal: Such was his devotion to righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his sense of honor.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部右侍郎，謚文忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of Rites and granted the posthumous title Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚文肅。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 吳麟征，字聖生，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Wu Linzheng, styled Shengsheng, was a man of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Linzheng, whose courtesy name was Shengsheng, came from Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 除建昌府推官，擒豪猾，捕劇盜，治聲日聞。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Jianchang Prefecture, captured powerful ruffians and major bandits, and his reputation for good governance spread daily.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating magistrate of Jianchang, he seized local bullies and captured notorious bandits, and his reputation as an able administrator grew by the day.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 補興化府，廉公有威，僚屬莫敢以私進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xinghua Prefecture, where his integrity and authority were such that subordinates dared not approach him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Xinghua, where his probity and stern bearing kept subordinates from pressing private favors on him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年，擢吏科給事中，請罷內遣，言：「古用內臣以致亂，今用內臣以求治。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was promoted to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel, requesting an end to inner-court eunuch missions, and said: "In antiquity inner eunuchs were used and brought disorder; today inner eunuchs are used in hopes of good government.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen he was made a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel and urged an end to eunuch missions, saying, "In old times eunuchs were employed and brought chaos; now they are employed in the hope of good government.

sentences.zh: 君之於臣，猶父之於子，未有信仆從，舍其子，求家之理者。」

translations.literal: A ruler toward his ministers is like a father toward his sons; never yet has one trusted servants, set aside his sons, and sought to put the household in order.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's relation to his ministers is like a father's to his sons; no one has ever trusted servants, turned away from his own sons, and still expected to govern the family well.

sentences.zh: 又言：「安民之本在守令。

translations.literal: He also said: "The foundation of pacifying the people lies in prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The key to securing the people lies in prefects and county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 郡守廉，縣令不敢貪；

translations.literal: When the prefect is incorrupt, magistrates dare not be greedy;
translations.idiomatic: If the prefect is honest, magistrates will not dare to steal;

sentences.zh: 郡守慈，縣令不敢虐；

translations.literal: when the prefect is merciful, magistrates dare not be cruel;
translations.idiomatic: if the prefect is humane, magistrates will not dare to abuse the people;

sentences.zh: 郡守精明，縣令不敢叢脞。

translations.literal: when the prefect is sharp, magistrates dare not be negligent and petty.
translations.idiomatic: if the prefect is vigilant, magistrates will not dare to fob off their duties in petty ways.

sentences.zh: 宜仿宣宗用況鐘故事，精擇而禮遣之，重以璽書，假便宜久任。

translations.literal: We should follow the Xuande emperor's precedent in employing Kuang Zhong: choose carefully and send them forth with ceremony, reinforce them with sealed imperial letters, and grant discretionary powers for long tenure.
translations.idiomatic: The court should follow the Xuande emperor's example with Kuang Zhong—choose men carefully, send them out with honor, empower them with sealed edicts, and let them serve long terms with broad discretion.

sentences.zh: 民生疾苦，吏治臧否，使得自達天子。」

translations.literal: The people's hardships and whether officialdom is good or bad would then reach the Son of Heaven directly."
translations.idiomatic: Then the people's suffering and the true state of local government could reach the emperor without obstruction."

sentences.zh: 時不能行。

translations.literal: At the time this could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: At the time nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 麟征在諫垣，直聲甚著。

translations.literal: While Linzheng served in the remonstrance offices, his reputation for blunt honesty was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In the censorate Linzheng became widely known for his outspoken integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋上疏乞假葬父。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he submitted a memorial requesting leave to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he memorialized the throne asking leave to return home and bury his father.

sentences.zh: 既去，貽言路公揭，謂：「自言官積輕，廟堂之上往往反其言而用之。

translations.literal: After he left he sent an open letter to the censorial community, saying: "They say that remonstrance officials carry little weight, yet those above the hall often do the opposite of what they advise.
translations.idiomatic: On leaving office he addressed an open letter to his colleagues in the censorate, saying, "People say remonstrance officials count for little, yet those in power often do the very opposite of what we urge.

sentences.zh: 奸人窺見此旨，明告君父，目為朋黨，自稱孤立，下背公論，上竊主權。

translations.literal: Villains perceive this and plainly tell the ruler and father, labeling others as factions while calling themselves isolated, betraying public opinion below and usurping the sovereign's power above.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty men see this and tell the emperor plainly that their rivals form factions while they alone are loyal; they defy public opinion below and seize power from the throne above.

sentences.zh: 諸君子宜盡化沾沾之意，毋落其彀中，使清流之禍再見明時。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen should wholly put aside petty contentiousness, not fall into their snare, and not let the calamity of the Pure Stream faction recur in our bright age.
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen should cast off all petty factional zeal and not fall into their trap, lest the disasters of the Pure Stream faction be repeated in our own day.

sentences.zh: 居久之，還朝。

translations.literal: After a long interval he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: After a long stay at home he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 劾吏部尚書田唯嘉贓汙，唯嘉罷去。

translations.literal: He impeached Minister of Personnel Tian Weijia for corruption; Weijia was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Tian Weijia, Minister of Personnel, for bribery, and Tian was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑科給事中，丁繼母憂。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments and entered mourning for his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to supervising secretary in the Bureau of Punishments, then went into mourning for his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起吏科都給事中，時貨賂公行，銓曹資格盡廢。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel; at the time bribery was rampant and seniority rules in the Board of Appointments were wholly abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was recalled as chief supervising secretary in the Bureau of Personnel, at a time when graft was everywhere and the Board of Appointments had cast aside all seniority rules.

sentences.zh: 麟征上言：「限年平配，固銓政之弊，然舍此無以待中才。

translations.literal: Linzheng memorialized: "Fixed-term rotation is indeed a flaw in appointment policy, yet without it there is no way to accommodate men of middling talent.
translations.idiomatic: Linzheng submitted a memorial saying, "Time-limited rotation is certainly a defect in personnel policy, but without it there is no orderly way to advance men of average ability.

sentences.zh: 今遷轉如流，不循資格，巧者速化，拙者積薪，開奔競之門，無益軍國之計。」

translations.literal: Now promotions flow like water without regard to seniority; the clever rise swiftly while the dull pile up like kindling, opening the gate to frantic competition and doing no good for military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Today appointments change as fast as a stream, with no regard for seniority; the clever advance overnight while the slow are left stacked like firewood, opening the door to frantic office-seeking and doing nothing for army or state.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor strongly approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，推太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year he was nominated Vice Minister of Rites in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year he was recommended for Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊薄京師。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels were at the gates of the capital.

sentences.zh: 麟征奉命守西直門。

translations.literal: Linzheng was ordered to defend the Xizhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Linzheng was ordered to hold the Xizhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 門當賊沖，賊詐為勤王兵求入。

translations.literal: The gate faced the main rebel thrust; the bandits pretended to be relief troops coming to save the throne and asked to be admitted.
translations.idiomatic: The gate lay in the rebels' main line of attack; they disguised themselves as troops coming to relieve the capital and asked to be let in.

sentences.zh: 中官欲納之，麟征不可，以土石堅塞其門，募死士縋城襲擊之，多所斬獲。

translations.literal: Eunuchs wished to admit them; Linzheng refused, blocked the gate solidly with earth and stone, recruited dare-to-die men to be lowered from the wall to strike them, and killed or captured many.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs wanted to let them in, but Linzheng refused; he packed the gate tight with earth and stone, raised volunteers to be lowered from the wall on ropes to attack the enemy, and killed or captured many.

sentences.zh: 賊攻益急，麟徵趨入朝，欲見帝白事。

translations.literal: As the rebel assault grew fiercer Linzheng hurried into court, wishing to see the emperor and report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel assault grew fiercer, and Linzheng rushed to court hoping to see the emperor and report what was happening.

sentences.zh: 至午門，魏藻德引麟征手曰：「國家如天之福，必無他虞。

translations.literal: At the Meridian Gate Wei Zaode took Linzheng by the hand and said: "The state enjoys heaven's blessing; there can be no other worry.
translations.idiomatic: At the Meridian Gate Wei Zaode took his hand and said, "The dynasty enjoys heaven's protection; there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 旦夕兵餉集，公何遽為？」

translations.literal: Troops and supplies will gather within days—why are you in such haste?
translations.idiomatic: Troops and supplies will arrive any day now—why are you in such a hurry?

sentences.zh: 引之出，遂還西直門。

translations.literal: He led him out, and Linzheng then returned to the Xizhi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He led him away, and Linzheng went back to the Xizhi Gate.

sentences.zh: 明日城陷，欲還邸，已為賊所據。

translations.literal: The next day the city fell; wishing to return to his residence, he found it already occupied by the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell; when he tried to go home he found his house already in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 乃入道旁祠，作書訣家人曰：「祖宗二百七十余年宗社，一旦至此，雖上有亢龍之悔，下有魚爛之殃，而身居諫垣，無所匡救，法當褫服。

translations.literal: He then entered a roadside shrine and wrote a farewell to his family: "Our ancestors' altar-state of more than two hundred and seventy years has come to this in a single day. Though above there is the regret of the dragon soaring too high and below the ruin of fish rotting from the head, I held office in the remonstrance bureaus yet could offer no rescue—by law I should strip off my robes.
translations.idiomatic: He went into a roadside shrine and wrote a farewell letter to his family: "The ancestral realm of more than two hundred and seventy years has collapsed in a day. Though the throne bears the regret of a dragon that has risen too high and the people suffer ruin from the head down, I served in the censorate yet could save nothing—by right I should lay aside my official robes.

sentences.zh: 殮用角巾青衫，覆以單衾，以誌吾哀。」

translations.literal: For my encoffinment use a kerchief cap and blue gown, covered with a single quilt, to mark my grief.
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in a scholar's cap and plain blue robe, covered with a single quilt, to show my sorrow.

sentences.zh: 解帶自經。

translations.literal: He loosened his belt and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He untied his belt and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 家人救之蘇，環泣請曰：「待祝孝廉至，一訣可乎？」

translations.literal: His family revived him; they wept around him and begged: "May we wait until the filial scholar Zhu arrives for one farewell?
translations.idiomatic: His family revived him; they gathered round weeping and asked, "May we wait until Zhu the filial scholar comes so you can take leave of him?

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He consented.

sentences.zh: 祝孝廉名淵，嘗救劉宗周下獄，與麟征善者也。

translations.literal: The filial scholar Zhu was named Yuan; he had once rescued Liu Zongzhou from imprisonment and was on friendly terms with Linzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The filial scholar Zhu, whose given name was Yuan, had once helped free Liu Zongzhou from prison and was a close friend of Linzheng.

sentences.zh: 明日，淵至。

translations.literal: The next day Yuan arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhu Yuan came.

sentences.zh: 麟征慷慨曰：「憶登第時夢隱士劉宗周吟文信國《零丁洋詩》，今山河碎矣，不死何為！」

translations.literal: Linzheng said with passion: "I recall that when I passed the examinations I dreamed of the recluse Liu Zongzhou reciting Wen Tianxiang's poem 'Song of the Lonely Sea'; now mountains and rivers are shattered—if I do not die, what am I for!
translations.idiomatic: Linzheng said fervently, "When I passed the examinations I dreamed of Liu Zongzhou reciting Wen Tianxiang's 'Song of the Lonely Sea'; now the realm lies in ruins—what reason is there to live on!

sentences.zh: 酌酒與淵別，遂自經，淵為視含殮而去。

translations.literal: He poured wine and took leave of Yuan, then hanged himself; Yuan arranged the placing of the pearl in his mouth and the encoffinment and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He shared a cup of wine in farewell with Zhu Yuan, then hanged himself; Yuan saw to his burial rites and left.

sentences.zh: 贈兵部右侍郎，謚忠節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of War and given the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Vice Minister of War and granted the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚貞肅。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Zhensu.

sentences.zh: 方賊之陷山西也，薊遼總督王永吉請撤寧遠吳三桂兵守關門，選士卒西行遏寇，即京師警，旦夕可援。

translations.literal: When the bandits were overrunning Shanxi, Grand Coordinator of Jiliao Wang Yongji requested that Wu Sangui's troops be withdrawn from Ningyuan to guard the passes, with picked soldiers sent west to check the bandits so that when the capital was alarmed relief could arrive within days.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were overrunning Shanxi, Wang Yongji, grand coordinator of Jiliao, proposed withdrawing Wu Sangui's army from Ningyuan to hold the passes and sending picked troops west to block the rebels, so that once the capital was threatened reinforcements could arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 天子下其議，麟征深然之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven referred the proposal for discussion; Linzheng strongly approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the proposal debated, and Linzheng strongly endorsed it.

sentences.zh: 輔臣陳演、魏藻德不可，謂：「無故棄地二百里，臣不敢任其咎。」

translations.literal: Chief ministers Chen Yan and Wei Zaode objected, saying: "To abandon two hundred li of territory without cause—your servant dare not bear that blame.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Chen Yan and Wei Zaode opposed it, saying, "To give up two hundred li of territory for no reason—we dare not take responsibility for that.

sentences.zh: 引漢棄涼州為證。

translations.literal: They cited the Han dynasty's abandonment of Liangzhou as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They cited the Han precedent of abandoning Liangzhou as proof.

sentences.zh: 麟征復為議數百言，六科不署名，獨疏昌言，弗省。

translations.literal: Linzheng again submitted a discussion of several hundred words; the six supervising-secretary bureaus would not sign, but he alone memorialized boldly, and it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Linzheng submitted another memorial of several hundred words; the six censorial bureaus refused to co-sign, but he spoke out alone in a separate memorial, and the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 及烽煙徹大內，帝始悔不用麟征言，旨下永吉，永吉馳出關，徙寧遠五十萬眾，日行數十里，十六日入關，二十日抵豐潤，而京師已陷矣。

translations.literal: When beacon fires reached the inner palace the emperor at last regretted not having followed Linzheng's advice; an edict went down to Yongji, who galloped out of the pass and moved five hundred thousand men from Ningyuan, marching several tens of li a day; on the sixteenth they entered the pass, on the twentieth they reached Fengrun—and the capital had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: When alarm fires reached the inner palace the emperor finally regretted ignoring Linzheng; an order went to Wang Yongji, who galloped out of the pass and marched five hundred thousand men from Ningyuan at several tens of li a day; they entered the pass on the sixteenth and reached Fengrun on the twentieth—but Beijing had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 城破，八門齊啟，惟西直門堅塞不能通。

translations.literal: When the city fell all eight gates opened at once; only the Xizhi Gate, firmly blocked, could not be passed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell all eight gates were opened; only the Xizhi Gate, packed shut, could not be used.

sentences.zh: 至五月七日，集民夫發掘乃開。

translations.literal: Not until the seventh day of the fifth month were laborers gathered to dig it open.
translations.idiomatic: Only on the seventh day of the fifth month were laborers assembled to dig it clear.

sentences.zh: 劉理順，字復禮，杞縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Lishun, styled Fuli, was a man of Qi County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lishun, whose courtesy name was Fuli, came from Qi County.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中舉於鄉。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 十赴會試，至崇禎七年始中式。

translations.literal: He went ten times to the metropolitan examination and only in the seventh year of Chongzhen did he pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sat the metropolitan examination ten times before finally passing in the seventh year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 及廷對，帝親擢第一，還宮喜曰：「朕今日得一耆碩矣。」

translations.literal: At the palace examination the emperor personally placed him first; returning to the palace he said with delight: "Today I have gained a venerable elder.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace audience the emperor personally ranked him first; back in the palace he said joyfully, "Today I have found a seasoned scholar.

sentences.zh: 拜修撰。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 益勤學，非其人不與交。

translations.literal: He studied all the more diligently and would not associate with anyone unworthy of him.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself even more into study and would not keep company with anyone he did not respect.

sentences.zh: 十二年春，畿輔告警，疏陳作士氣、矜窮民、簡良吏、定師期、信賞罰、招脅從六事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twelfth year an alarm was raised in the metropolitan region; he submitted a memorial setting forth six measures: building soldiers' morale, showing compassion to the poor, selecting good officials, fixing campaign deadlines, trusting rewards and punishments, and winning over those coerced to follow the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of his twelfth year at court, with the capital districts under threat, he memorialized the throne on six urgent reforms: stiffen the army's spirit, relieve the destitute, appoint worthy magistrates, set firm dates for campaigns, make rewards and punishments credible, and induce defectors from the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 歷南京司業、左中允、右諭德，入侍經筵兼東宮講官。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Vice Director of Studies at Nanjing, Left Household Assistant, and Right Reader-in-Waiting, entering attendance at the Classics Lecture and serving concurrently as lecturer to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Nanjing Vice Director of Studies, Left Household Assistant, and Right Reader-in-Waiting, then entered the emperor's Classics Lecture and doubled as tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 楊嗣昌奪情入閣，理順昌言於朝，嗣昌奪其講官。

translations.literal: When Yang Sichang left mourning to enter the Grand Secretariat, Lishun spoke forthrightly at court; Sichang stripped him of his lectureship.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sichang had resumed office from mourning and joined the Grand Secretariat; Lishun spoke bluntly against him in open court, and Sichang removed him from his post as palace lecturer.

sentences.zh: 開封垂陷，理順建議河北設重臣，練敢死士為後圖，疏格不行。

translations.literal: As Kaifeng was on the verge of falling, Lishun proposed posting a high minister in Hebei and training dare-to-die troops as a reserve plan; his memorial was rejected and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: With Kaifeng nearly lost, Lishun urged placing a senior commander in Hebei and drilling suicide squads for a fallback strategy, but the memorial was blocked and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 嗣昌、薛國觀、周延儒叠用事，理順一無所附麗。

translations.literal: Sichang, Xue Guoguan, and Zhou Yanru held power in turn, yet Lishun attached himself to none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yang Sichang, Xue Guoguan, and Zhou Yanru dominated the government one after another, Lishun would not lean on any faction.

sentences.zh: 出溫體仁門，言論不少徇。

translations.literal: Though he had come from Wen Tiren's circle, in speech he did not much defer.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen under Wen Tiren, yet he rarely trimmed his words to please anyone.

sentences.zh: 賊犯京師急，守卒缺餉，陰雨饑凍。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed the capital urgently; the garrison lacked pay, and in steady rain they suffered hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel armies closed on Beijing; the defenders went unpaid, and endless rain left them hungry and freezing.

sentences.zh: 理順詣朝房語諸執政，急請帑，眾唯唯。

translations.literal: Lishun went to the morning chamber to speak with the chief ministers, urgently requesting treasury funds; the crowd only murmured assent.
translations.idiomatic: Lishun sought out the chief ministers in the morning hall and pleaded for an immediate grant from the treasury; they answered with vague, noncommittal noises.

sentences.zh: 理順太息歸，捐家貲犒守城卒。

translations.literal: Lishun sighed deeply and returned home, donating his family wealth to reward the city-garrison soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He went home with a deep sigh and spent his own fortune to treat the men defending the walls.

sentences.zh: 僚友問進止，正色曰：「存亡視國，尚須商酌耶！」

translations.literal: When colleagues asked what he would do, he said sternly: "Survival or ruin hangs on the fate of the state—need we still deliberate!
translations.idiomatic: Friends asked whether he would flee; he answered gravely, "Whether the dynasty lives or dies is at stake—what is there left to discuss?

sentences.zh: 城破，妻萬、妾李請先死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, his wife Wan and concubine Li asked to die first.
translations.idiomatic: After the walls were breached, his wife Wan and concubine Li begged to die before him.

sentences.zh: 既絕，理順大書曰：「成仁取義，孔、孟所傳。

translations.literal: When they had perished, Lishun wrote in large characters: "To achieve humanity and uphold righteousness is what Confucius and Mencius transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Once they were dead, Lishun wrote boldly: "To die for humanity and righteousness is the teaching Confucius and Mencius bequeathed.

sentences.zh: 文信踐之，吾何不然！」

translations.literal: Wen Xin practiced it—why should I not do the same!
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wen practiced it—why should I fall short!

sentences.zh: 書畢投繯，年六十三。

translations.literal: When he had finished writing he hanged himself; he was sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the lines and hanged himself. He was sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 仆四人皆從死。

translations.literal: Four servants all followed him in death.
translations.idiomatic: Four household servants died with him.

sentences.zh: 群盜多中州人，入唁曰：「此吾鄉杞縣劉狀元也，居鄉厚德，何遽死？」

translations.literal: Many of the bandits were men of the central provinces; they came in to offer condolences and said: "This is our fellow townsman, Liu the Metropolitan Graduate of Qi County—he lived in the village with deep virtue; why did he die so suddenly?
translations.idiomatic: Many rebels were natives of the central plain; they came to mourn and cried, "This is Liu the palace graduate from our Qi County—he was a man of great kindness at home; why did he have to die so soon?

sentences.zh: 羅拜號泣而去。

translations.literal: They bowed in a circle, weeping and wailing, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They kowtowed all around him, wailing, and left.

sentences.zh: 後贈詹事，謚文正。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wen Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was posthumously appointed Grand Mentor and honored with the temple name Wen Zheng.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚文烈。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Wen Lie.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Wen Lie.

sentences.zh: 汪偉，字叔度，休寧人，寄籍上元。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, styled Shudu, was a man of Xiuning, registered as a native of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, whose courtesy name was Shudu, came from Xiuning but was entered on the registers at Shangyuan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the first year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 十一年，由慈溪知縣行取。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was selected for capital service from his post as magistrate of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to the capital from his post as magistrate of Cixi.

sentences.zh: 帝以國家多故，朝臣詞苑起家，儒緩不習吏事，無以理紛禦變，改舊例，擇知推治行卓絕者入翰林。

translations.literal: Because the state faced many troubles, court ministers who rose from the literary academies were Confucian and slow and unpracticed in administrative affairs, unable to manage disorder and meet sudden change; the old rule was changed to choose magistrates and prefects of outstanding conduct for the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that in a time of crisis, officials drawn from the literary academies were too bookish and inexperienced in administration to handle chaos; he altered precedent and recruited into the Hanlin those local magistrates and prefects whose records were truly outstanding.

sentences.zh: 偉擢檢討，給假歸。

translations.literal: Wei was promoted to Hanlin Compiler and granted leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was made a Hanlin Compiler and given leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 還朝，充東宮講官。

translations.literal: Upon returning to court he served as lecturer to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he came back to the capital he was appointed tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 十六年，賊陷承天、荊、襄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year the bandits took Chengtian, Jing, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year rebels captured Chengtian and overran Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 偉以留都根本之地，上《江防綢繆疏》，言：「金陵城周圍百二十里，雖十萬眾不能守。

translations.literal: Because the southern capital was the root of the realm, Wei submitted the "Memorial on Meticulous Yangtze Defense," saying: "Jinling's walls run one hundred and twenty li in circuit; even a hundred thousand men could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, seeing Nanjing as the dynasty's last anchor, submitted his "Memorial on Thorough River Defense," arguing: "The walls of Jinling stretch one hundred and twenty li; no garrison of a hundred thousand could hold them.

sentences.zh: 議者謂無守城法，有防江法。

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter say there is no method of defending a city, but there is a method of defending a river.
translations.idiomatic: Strategists say the city cannot be defended—but the river can.

sentences.zh: 賊自北來，淮安為要；

translations.literal: If the bandits come from the north, Huai'an is the key point;
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy advances from the north, Huai'an is decisive;

sentences.zh: 自上遊來，九江為要；

translations.literal: if they come from upstream, Jiujiang is the key point;
translations.idiomatic: if from upstream, Jiujiang is decisive;

sentences.zh: 禦淮所以禦江，守九江所以守金陵也。

translations.literal: to defend the Huai is to defend the Yangtze, and to hold Jiujiang is to hold Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: holding the Huai defends the Yangtze, and holding Jiujiang defends Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 淮有史可法，屹然保障；

translations.literal: At the Huai, Shi Kefa stands firm as a bulwark;
translations.idiomatic: On the Huai front Shi Kefa already stands as a rock;

sentences.zh: 九江一郡，宜設重臣鎮之。

translations.literal: for the single prefecture of Jiujiang a high minister ought to be stationed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang prefecture alone needs a senior commander posted there.

sentences.zh: 自是而上之至於武昌，下之至於太平、采石、浦口，命南京兵部大臣建牙分閫，以接聲援，而金陵之門戶固矣。

translations.literal: From there upstream as far as Wuchang, and downstream as far as Taiping, Caishi, and Pukou, order ministers of the Nanjing Ministry of War to raise command banners and divide military districts, linking supporting forces, and then the gateways of Jinling will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: From Wuchang upstream to Taiping, Caishi, and Pukou downstream, ministers of the Nanjing Board of War should establish separate commands to relay reinforcements—then Nanjing's approaches will be secure.

sentences.zh: 南京兵部有重兵而無用，操江欲用兵而無人，宜使緩急相應。

translations.literal: The Nanjing Ministry of War has large forces but cannot use them; the Yangtze command wishes to use troops but has no men—urgent and slack situations ought to answer to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's war ministry commands troops it cannot deploy, while the river patrol needs men it does not have; the two branches should be made to act in concert when crisis strikes.

sentences.zh: 而府尹、府丞之官，重其權，久其任，聯百萬士民心，以分兵部操江之責。」

translations.literal: As for the offices of metropolitan magistrate and vice-magistrate, their authority should be weighted and their tenure lengthened, binding the hearts of a million people of scholar and commoner rank, to share the responsibilities of the Ministry of War and the Yangtze command.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged strengthening the metropolitan magistrate and vice-magistrate, giving them longer terms and real power to rally the city's gentry and commoners and share the burden now borne only by the war ministry and river command.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之，乃設九江總督。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it, and thereupon established the Jiujiang governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the plan and created the post of governor-general at Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 又言：「兵額既虧，宜以衛所官舍余丁補伍操練，修治兵船，以資防禦。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since military rolls are already depleted, the surplus sons of guard and battalion officers' households should fill the ranks for drill and training, and war vessels should be repaired for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed filling depleted rolls with surplus sons from military households, drilling them, and repairing warships for river defense.

sentences.zh: 額餉不足，暫借鹽課、漕米給之。」

translations.literal: Where allotted pay is insufficient, salt levies and grain transport rice should be borrowed temporarily to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Where regular pay fell short, salt revenues and transport grain could be advanced on loan to feed the troops.

sentences.zh: 所條奏皆切時務。

translations.literal: Every item he memorialized struck at the urgent business of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Each proposal addressed a pressing need of the hour.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，賊兵東犯。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year the bandit army marched east.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the third month, rebel forces drove eastward.

sentences.zh: 偉語閣臣：「事急矣，亟遣大僚守畿郡。

translations.literal: Wei told the Grand Secretaries: "The situation is desperate; send high ministers at once to guard the metropolitan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei told the Grand Secretaries, "Matters are critical—dispatch senior ministers immediately to hold the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 都中城守，文自內閣，武自公侯伯以下，各率子弟畫地守。

translations.literal: For defense within the capital, civil affairs should begin with the Grand Secretariat and military affairs with the dukes, marquises, and earls downward; each should lead his sons and younger relatives to guard an assigned sector of the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Beijing, civil officials from the Grand Secretariat down and military nobles from the dukes and marquises down should each lead their sons to defend assigned sections of the wall.

sentences.zh: 庶民統以紳士，家自為守。

translations.literal: The common people should be organized under local gentry, each household defending itself.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary townspeople should be grouped under local scholars, with every household responsible for its own defense.

sentences.zh: 而京軍分番巡僥，以待勤王之師。」

translations.literal: The capital garrison should patrol in rotation, awaiting the armies that will come to relieve the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Capital troops should patrol in shifts until relief armies arrive.

sentences.zh: 魏藻德笑曰：「大僚守畿輔，誰肯者？」

translations.literal: Wei Zaode laughed and said: "If high ministers are sent to guard the metropolitan region, who would be willing?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zaode laughed, "Send grand ministers to guard the suburbs? Who would go?"

sentences.zh: 偉曰：「此何等時，猶較尊卑、計安危耶？

translations.literal: Wei said: "What sort of time is this, that you still compare rank and calculate safety?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei replied, "At a moment like this you still weigh rank and personal safety?

sentences.zh: 請以一劇郡見委。」

translations.literal: Please assign me to one important commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Give me any serious prefecture and I will take it.

sentences.zh: 藻德哂其早計。

translations.literal: Zaode sneered at his premature planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zaode mocked him for planning too far ahead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，真定遊擊謝加福殺巡撫徐標迎賊。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhending guerrilla Xie Jiafu killed the grand coordinator Xu Biao and welcomed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Zhending irregular Xie Jiafu murdered Grand Coordinator Xu Biao and opened the city to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 偉泣曰：「事至此乎！」

translations.literal: Wei wept and said: "Has it come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Wei wept, "So it has come to this!

sentences.zh: 作書寄友人曰：「賊據真定，奸人滿都城，外郡上供絲粟不至，諸臣無一可支危亡者，如聖主何！

translations.literal: He wrote to a friend: "The bandits hold Zhending, traitors fill the capital, tribute of silk and grain from outer commanderies no longer arrives, and among the ministers there is not one who can shore up imminent ruin—what is to become of our sage lord!
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a friend: "The rebels hold Zhending, collaborators throng the capital, grain and silk from the provinces no longer reach us, and not one minister can stave off collapse—what will become of the Son of Heaven?

sentences.zh: 平時誤國之人，終日言門戶而不顧朝廷，今當何處伸狂喙耶！」

translations.literal: Those who have ruined the state in peacetime talk all day of faction and never look to the court—where will they now stretch their reckless tongues!
translations.idiomatic: The men who ruined us in easier days chatter about factions and ignore the throne—where will they wag their tongues now?

sentences.zh: 賊薄都城，守兵乏餉，不得食，偉市餅餌以饋。

translations.literal: When the bandits pressed the capital the garrison lacked pay and could not eat; Wei bought cakes and biscuits to feed them.
translations.idiomatic: As rebels closed on Beijing the defenders went hungry for lack of pay; Wei bought bread and cakes to feed them.

sentences.zh: 已而城陷，偉歸寓，語繼室耿善撫幼子。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; Wei returned to his lodging and told his stepwife Geng to care well for their young son.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he went home and told his stepwife Geng to look after their little boy.

sentences.zh: 耿泣曰：「我獨不能從公死乎！」

translations.literal: Geng wept and said: "Can I alone not follow you in death!
translations.idiomatic: Geng wept, "Must I alone be left behind?

sentences.zh: 因以幼子屬其弟，衣新衣，上下縫，引刀自剄不殊，復投繯遂絕，時年二十三。

translations.literal: She thereupon entrusted the infant to his younger brother, put on new clothes sewn shut above and below, cut her throat but did not die, then hanged herself and expired; she was twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: She handed the child to his brother, dressed in new garments sewn shut at neck and hem, slashed her throat without success, then hanged herself until she was dead. She was twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 偉欣然曰：「是成吾志。」

translations.literal: Wei said with satisfaction: "This fulfills my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Wei said gladly, "Now my wish is fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 移其屍於堂，貽子觀書，勉以忠孝，乃自經。

translations.literal: He moved her body to the hall, left his son with books to study, exhorted him with loyalty and filial piety, and then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He laid her in the main hall, set books before his son and charged him with loyalty and filial duty, then hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 贈少詹事，謚文烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Grand Mentor and given the posthumous title Wen Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Grand Mentor with the temple name Wen Lie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚文毅。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Wen Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Wen Yi.

sentences.zh: 吳甘來，字和受，江西新昌人。

translations.literal: Wu Ganlai, styled Heshou, was a man of Xinchang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ganlai, whose courtesy name was Heshou, came from Xinchang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 父之才，西安府同知。

translations.literal: His father Zhicai was Assistant Administration Commissioner of Xi'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhicai served as vice commissioner of the Xi'an prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 甘來與兄泰來同舉鄉試。

translations.literal: Ganlai and his elder brother Tailai passed the provincial examination together.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlai and his elder brother Tailai qualified together in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，甘來成進士，授中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the inaugural year of Chongzhen, Ganlai passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Chongzhen reign Ganlai took the jinshi and was appointed a Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 後三年，泰來亦成進士，授南京太常博士。

translations.literal: Three years later Tailai also passed the jinshi examination and was appointed Erudite of the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Tailai also passed the jinshi and was made an erudite at the Nanjing Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 五年，甘來擢刑科給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ganlai was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Penal Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ganlai was promoted to supervising secretary of the Penal Section.

sentences.zh: 七年，西北大旱，秦、晉人相食，疏請發粟以振，而言：「山西總兵張應昌等半殺難民以冒功，中州諸郡畏曹變蛟兵甚於賊。

translations.literal: In the seventh year a great drought struck the northwest; people in Qin and Jin ate one another; he memorialized requesting grain relief to succor them, and said: "Regional commanders such as Zhang Yingchang of Shanxi killed refugees by halves to claim merit, and in the central provinces the people feared Cao Bianjiao's troops more than the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year severe drought ravaged the northwest; in Shaanxi and Shanxi people cannibalized one another. He asked that grain be released for relief and wrote: "Commanders like Zhang Yingchang in Shanxi butchered refugees wholesale to pad their reports, while in the heartland the people feared Cao Bianjiao's soldiers more than the rebels.

sentences.zh: 陛下生之而不能，武臣殺之而不顧，臣實痛之。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty gives them life yet cannot save them; military men kill them without regard—I am truly pained.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty would preserve them yet cannot; your generals slaughter them without consequence. This grieves me deeply.

sentences.zh: 又言：「賞罰者，將將大機權也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Rewards and punishments are the great pivot by which a commander commands his commanders.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Reward and punishment are the lever by which one general commands another.

sentences.zh: 陛下加意邊陲，賞無延格。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has paid close attention to the frontier and grants rewards without delay.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has lavished care on the borders and grants rewards without delay.

sentences.zh: 乃紅夷獻俘，黔、蜀爭功，昌黎死守，功猶待勘，急則用其死綏，緩則束以文法。

translations.literal: Yet when the red-haired barbarians presented captives, Qian and Shu vied over credit; Changli was stubbornly defended yet merit still awaits verification; in urgency one uses men who die in loyalty, in slackness one binds them with civil law.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Dutch prisoners were presented, Guizhou and Sichuan quarreled over credit; Changli was heroically held yet merit still awaits review; in crisis you demand death in battle, in calm you bind men with bureaucratic rules.

sentences.zh: 且封疆之罰，武與文二，內與外二，士卒與將帥二。

translations.literal: Moreover, punishments on the frontier are twofold for civil and military, twofold for inner and outer, and twofold for soldiers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier justice, moreover, is one standard for civil officials and another for soldiers, one for the capital and another for the field, one for common troops and another for commanders.

sentences.zh: 受命建牙，或逮或逐，以封疆罪罪之；

translations.literal: Once commissioned with command banners, some are seized and some driven off, punished with frontier crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Men given independent commands are seized or dismissed for border offenses;

sentences.zh: 而跋扈將帥，罪狀已暴，止於戴罪。

translations.literal: yet overbearing generals, though their crimes are already exposed, are only made to hold office while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: yet arrogant generals whose guilt is plain are merely allowed to serve on probation.

sentences.zh: 偏裨不能令士卒，將帥不能令偏裨，督撫不能令將帥，將聽賊自來自去，誰為陛下翦兇逆者？」

translations.literal: Junior officers cannot command soldiers, generals cannot command junior officers, governors cannot command generals—then the army will watch the bandits come and go as they please; who for Your Majesty will cut down the violent and rebellious?
translations.idiomatic: Company officers cannot control their men, generals cannot control company officers, governors cannot control generals—troops will let the enemy come and go at will. Who then will destroy the rebels for Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起吏科，進兵科右給事中，乞假歸。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was reappointed to the Personnel Section, advanced to Right Supervising Secretary of the Military Section, and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned as supervising secretary of the Personnel Section, was promoted to right supervising secretary of the Military Section, and took leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，起歷戶科都給事中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was recalled and served in succession as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled and rose to chief supervising secretary of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 中外多故，荊、襄數郡，賊未至而撫道諸臣率稱護藩以去。

translations.literal: Within and without there were many troubles; in several commanderies of Jing and Xiang the bandits had not yet arrived, yet grand coordinators and circuit intendants generally claimed they were escorting princes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Troubles multiplied at home and abroad; in several districts of Jing and Xiang the rebels had not even arrived, yet governors and circuit intendants routinely claimed they were escorting princes and fled.

sentences.zh: 甘來曰：「若爾，則是棄地方而逃也。

translations.literal: Ganlai said: "If that is so, then they are abandoning their territories and fleeing.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlai said, "If that is allowed, officials are simply abandoning their posts and running.

sentences.zh: 城社人民，誰與守者？」

translations.literal: The altars of state and the people—who will remain to defend them?
translations.idiomatic: Who will guard the land and the people?

sentences.zh: 乃上疏曰：「天子眾建親親，將使屏藩帝室，故曰『宗子維城』。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "The Son of Heaven establishes many kinsmen in kinship so that they may screen and protect the imperial house—hence it is said, 'The sons of the clan are walls of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "The Son of Heaven multiplies princes of the blood so they may shield the throne—thus the ode says, 'The royal sons are the city's walls.

sentences.zh: 乃烽火才傳，一朝委去以為民望，而諸臣猶嘵嘵以擁衛自功，掩其失地之罪。

translations.literal: Yet as soon as beacon fires were reported they cast everything aside in a morning and departed, setting the people's expectation, while the ministers still clamored that escorting princes was their achievement, covering the crime of lost territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at the first beacon they fled in a morning, abandoning the people they were sworn to protect, while the same officials boasted of 'escorting' princes to mask their surrender of whole districts.

sentences.zh: 是維城為可留可去之人，名都為可守可棄之土，撫道為可有可無之官。

translations.literal: Thus the walls of the city became people who might stay or leave, famous capitals became soil that might be held or cast away, and grand coordinators became offices that might exist or not.
translations.idiomatic: The 'walls' became optional, great cities disposable, and frontier governors a luxury the court could take or leave.

sentences.zh: 功罪不明，賞罰不著，莫此為甚！」

translations.literal: Merit and guilt unclear, rewards and punishments not fixed—nothing exceeds this!'
translations.idiomatic: With merit and guilt undistinguished and reward and punishment unsettled, nothing could be worse.'

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝大嘉嘆。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor greatly praised and sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and praised it warmly.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝詰戶部尚書倪元璐餉額，甘來曰：「臣科與戶曹表裏，餉可按籍稽。

translations.literal: One day the emperor questioned Revenue Minister Ni Yuanlu about ration quotas; Ganlai said: "My section and the revenue bureau are inner and outer to each other; rations can be checked against the registers.
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor pressed Revenue Minister Ni Yuanlu on grain quotas; Ganlai said, "My office works hand in glove with the ministry; supplies can be verified against the rolls.

sentences.zh: 臣所慮者，兵聞賊而逃，民見賊而喜，恐非無餉之患，而無民之患。

translations.literal: What I fear is that soldiers flee at the sound of bandits while the people rejoice at the sight of bandits—I fear the affliction is not lack of pay but lack of the people.
translations.idiomatic: What troubles me is that troops run when they hear rebels while commoners cheer when they see them—the danger is not empty granaries but empty allegiance.

sentences.zh: 宜急輕賦稅，收人心。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to lighten taxes and levies quickly and recover the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Light taxes at once and win the people back.

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded in assent.

sentences.zh: 甘來遘疾，連請告。

translations.literal: Ganlai fell ill and repeatedly requested leave.
translations.idiomatic: Ganlai fell ill and repeatedly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 會帝命編修陳名夏掌戶科，甘來喜得代。

translations.literal: Just then the emperor ordered Compiler Chen Mingxia to take charge of the Revenue Section; Ganlai was glad to have a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Compiler Chen Mingxia to head the Revenue Section; Ganlai was relieved to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 不數日，賊薄都城。

translations.literal: Within a few days the bandits pressed the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Within days rebels were at the walls of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 時泰來官禮部員外郎矣，甘來屬兄歸事母，而自誓必死。

translations.literal: By then Tailai was an Outer Court Secretary in the Ministry of Rites; Ganlai charged his brother to return and serve their mother, while he himself vowed he would certainly die.
translations.idiomatic: Tailai was by then a secretary in the Ministry of Rites; Ganlai told his brother to go home and care for their mother while he himself swore to die.

sentences.zh: 明日，城陷，有言駕南幸者，甘來曰：「主上明決，必不輕出。」

translations.literal: The next day the city fell; some said the imperial carriage would go south in felicity; Ganlai said: "Our lord is clear and resolute; he will certainly not leave lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the city fell; some said the emperor would flee south; Ganlai said, "The sovereign is clear-minded and resolute; he will not lightly abandon the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃疾走皇城，不得入。

translations.literal: He then ran swiftly to the Imperial City but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to the Forbidden City but could not get in.

sentences.zh: 返檢幾上疏草曰：「當賊寇縱橫，徒持議論，無益豪末。」

translations.literal: Returning, he looked over draft memorials on his desk and said: "When bandits rampage everywhere, to hold only to debate is of no use even to a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Back at his desk he looked over draft memorials and said, "With rebels running riot, talk alone is worthless.

sentences.zh: 盡取焚之，毋釣後世名，遂投繯死。

translations.literal: He took them all and burned them, not angling for a name in later ages, and then hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He burned every draft, unwilling to fish for posthumous fame, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 贈太常卿，謚忠節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and given the posthumous title Zhong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with the temple name Zhong Jie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚莊介。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Zhuang Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Zhuang Jie.

sentences.zh: 王章，字漢臣，武進人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang, courtesy name Hanchen, was a native of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang, styled Hanchen, came from Wujin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the first year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 授諸暨知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 少孤，母訓之嚴。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother instructed him strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early, and his mother raised him with strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 及為令，祖帳歸少暮，母訶跪予杖，曰：「朝廷以百里授酒人乎！」

translations.literal: When he became magistrate, a farewell banquet was held; he returned somewhat late at dusk; his mother rebuked him, knelt, and handed him a staff, saying: "Did the court invest a hundred-li district in a wine-server!
translations.idiomatic: After he took office, the people gave him a send-off; he came home rather late one evening. His mother scolded him, knelt, and offered him a cane, saying, "Did the court give you charge of a district so you could play the wine-server?

sentences.zh: 章伏地不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Zhang lay prostrate and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang prostrated himself and would not raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 親友為力解，乃已。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends pleaded earnestly on his behalf, and only then did she stop.
translations.idiomatic: Kin and friends interceded vigorously before she relented.

sentences.zh: 治諸暨有聲。

translations.literal: His governance of Zhuji won renown.
translations.idiomatic: He won a strong reputation governing Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 甫半歲，以才調鄞縣。

translations.literal: Barely half a year later, on account of his talent he was transferred to Yin County.
translations.idiomatic: After only half a year his ability won him a transfer to Yin County.

sentences.zh: 諸暨民與鄞民爭挽章，至相嘩。

translations.literal: The people of Zhuji and the people of Yin vied to detain Zhang, until they shouted at one another.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Zhuji and Yin competed to keep him, coming to open quarrels.

sentences.zh: 治鄞益有聲，數註上考。

translations.literal: His rule of Yin grew still more renowned, and he repeatedly received top merit evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation in Yin grew stronger still, and he repeatedly earned the highest performance ratings.

sentences.zh: 十一年，行取入都。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was selected by special promotion and entered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen he was promoted to the capital through the direct-selection process.

sentences.zh: 時有考選翰林之命，行取者爭奔競，給事中陳啟新論之。

translations.literal: At the time there was an order for examination and selection into the Hanlin Academy; those promoted by selection strove in frantic competition; Supervising Secretary Chen Qixin remonstrated on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order called for exams to fill Hanlin posts, and the newly selected officials scrambled for appointment. Supervising Secretary Chen Qixin criticized the rush.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，命吏部上訪冊，罪廷臣濫徇者。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to submit an investigative register, punishing court ministers who had indulged and favored others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered the Ministry of Personnel to submit a review dossier to punish court ministers who had improperly favored candidates.

sentences.zh: 尚書姜逢元、王業浩，給事中傅元初，御史禹好善等六人閑住；

translations.literal: Ministers Jiang Fengyuan and Wang Yehao, Supervising Secretary Fu Yuanchu, Censor Yu Haoshan, and six others in all were ordered to idle at home;
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Jiang Fengyuan and Wang Yehao, Supervising Secretary Fu Yuanchu, Censor Yu Haoshan, and five others—a total of six—were suspended from office;

sentences.zh: 給事中孫晉、御史李右讜等三人降調；

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Sun Jin, Censor Li Youdan, and three others in all were demoted and transferred;
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Sun Jin, Censor Li Youdan, and one other—a total of three—were demoted and reassigned;

sentences.zh: 給事中劉含輝、御史劉興秀等十一人貶二秩視事。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liu Huihui, Censor Liu Xingxiu, and eleven others in all were demoted two ranks but continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Huihui, Censor Liu Xingxiu, and nine others—a total of eleven—were demoted two grades but kept their posts.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書田維嘉等乃請先推部曹，凡推二十二人，章與焉，授工部主事。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Tian Weijia and others then requested that departmental clerks be recommended first; twenty-two men were recommended in all, Zhang among them, and he was given appointment as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Tian Weijia and his colleagues then proposed promoting bureau staff first. Twenty-two men were nominated, Zhang among them, and he received appointment as principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 章及任浚、塗必泓、李嗣京欲疏辨，憚為首獲罪。

translations.literal: Zhang, along with Ren Jun, Tu Bihong, and Li Sijing, wished to submit a memorial in explanation but feared being first to incur guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Ren Jun, Tu Bihong, and Li Sijing wanted to submit a memorial clearing their names but feared whoever went first would be punished.

sentences.zh: 李士淳者耄矣，四人不告而首其名，士淳知之，懼且怒，與章等大詬。

translations.literal: Li Shichun was already advanced in years; the four men, without telling him, put his name first; learning of it, Shichun was both frightened and angry, and he bitterly reviled Zhang and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shichun was very old. The four men listed his name first without telling him. When he found out he was both afraid and furious, and he cursed Zhang and the others roundly.

sentences.zh: 而帝知維嘉有私，詔許與考。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor knew Weijia had shown favoritism and issued an edict permitting them to take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor knew Tian had acted with bias, and ordered that the candidates be allowed to sit for the exam.

sentences.zh: 又以為首者必良士也，擢士淳編修，章等皆御史。

translations.literal: The emperor also thought that whoever was placed first must be a worthy man; Shichun was elevated to Hanlin Compiler, and Zhang and the others all became censors.
translations.idiomatic: He also assumed whoever had been listed first must be a man of merit: Shichun was made Hanlin compiler, and Zhang and the others were all appointed censors.

sentences.zh: 章上疏請罷內操，寬江南逋賦。

translations.literal: Zhang submitted a memorial requesting that internal drill troops be abolished and delinquent grain levies in Jiangnan be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang memorialized asking that palace drill units be abolished and arrears on Jiangnan land taxes be remitted.

sentences.zh: 明年出按甘肅，持風紀，飭邊防。

translations.literal: The next year he was sent out to tour Gansu, upholding regulations and discipline, and rectifying frontier defenses.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was dispatched to inspect Gansu, enforcing discipline and tightening frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 西部寇莊浪，巡撫急征兵。

translations.literal: Western tribes raided Zhuanglang; the grand coordinator urgently raised troops.
translations.idiomatic: Western tribes raided Zhuanglang, and the grand coordinator urgently called up troops.

sentences.zh: 章曰：「貧寇索食耳。」

translations.literal: Zhang said: "They are poor raiders seeking food, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said, "They are poor bandits looking for food, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 策馬入其帳，眾羅拜乞降，乃稍給之食。

translations.literal: He spurred his horse into their camp; the whole band knelt and bowed, begging to surrender, and he then gave them a little food.
translations.idiomatic: He rode into their camp; they bowed in ranks begging to submit, and he gave them a little food.

sentences.zh: 兩河旱，章檄城隍神：「御史受錢或戕害人，神殛御史，毋虐民。

translations.literal: When drought struck the two river regions, Zhang issued a written summons to the city-god: "If a censor takes bribes or harms people, let the god strike the censor down; do not torment the people.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the region, Zhang wrote to the city god: "If a censor takes bribes or kills the innocent, let heaven strike him down—not the common people.

sentences.zh: 神血食茲土，不能請上帝蘇一方，當奏天子易爾位。」

translations.literal: You, god, receive blood-sacrifice on this soil; if you cannot ask the Supreme Lord to revive this region, you ought to memorialize the Son of Heaven to replace your post.
translations.idiomatic: You feast on offerings in this land—if you cannot appeal to Heaven to save the people, I shall memorialize the emperor to replace you.

sentences.zh: 檄焚，雨大註。

translations.literal: The summons was burned, and rain poured down.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the summons; rain came down in torrents.

sentences.zh: 邊卒貸武弁金，償以賊首，武弁以冒功，坐是數召邊釁。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers borrowed money from military officers and repaid it with bandit heads; officers used this to claim false merit, and for this reason border clashes were repeatedly provoked.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier soldiers borrowed from officers and paid them back with enemy heads; the officers used these to claim false victories, which repeatedly stirred border fighting.

sentences.zh: 章著令，非大舉毋得以零級冒功。

translations.literal: Zhang promulgated an order that without a major campaign one might not claim merit with fragmentary grades.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang issued regulations: without a major campaign, petty kill-counts could not be used to claim merit.

sentences.zh: 劾罷巡撫劉鎬貪惰。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed Grand Coordinator Liu Hao for greed and sloth.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and dismissed Grand Coordinator Liu Hao for corruption and sloth.

sentences.zh: 又所部十道監司，劾罷其四。

translations.literal: Again, of the ten circuit supervising officials in his jurisdiction, he impeached and removed four.
translations.idiomatic: Of the ten provincial overseers under his authority, he drove four from office.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he returned home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 服闋，還朝，巡視京營，按籍額軍十一萬有奇。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to court, inspected the capital armies, and according to the registers the quota troops numbered a little over one hundred eleven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned and inspected the metropolitan garrison; the rolls listed somewhat more than 111,000 troops on paper.

sentences.zh: 喜曰：「兵至十萬，猶可為也。」

translations.literal: Delighted, he said: "With troops reaching a hundred thousand, something can still be done.
translations.idiomatic: He said with satisfaction, "With a hundred thousand men we might still manage something.

sentences.zh: 及閱視，半死者，余冒伍，憊甚，矢折刀缺，聞炮聲掩耳，馬未馳輒墮。

translations.literal: When he came to inspection, half were dead, the remainder padded the rolls; they were utterly exhausted, arrows broken and blades chipped, and at the sound of cannon they covered their ears; before the horse had broken into a gallop they fell off.
translations.idiomatic: But on inspection half were ghosts on the roster, the rest were padding: they were spent—broken arrows, notched blades—and at cannon fire they covered their ears; they fell before their horses could break into a run.

sentences.zh: 而司農缺餉，半歲不發。

translations.literal: Yet the Ministry of Revenue lacked funds for pay, and for half a year none was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the treasury could not cover pay; none had been issued for half a year.

sentences.zh: 章屢疏請帑，不報。

translations.literal: Zhang repeatedly memorialized requesting funds from the treasury, but received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang repeatedly asked for emergency funds; the throne never answered.

sentences.zh: 逾月，賊陷真定，京師大震。

translations.literal: More than a month later the bandits took Zhending; the capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the rebels took Zhending, and panic seized the capital.

sentences.zh: 襄城伯李國禎發營卒五萬營城外，章與給事中光時亨守阜成門。

translations.literal: Duke of Xiangcheng Li Guozhen sent fifty thousand garrison troops to encamp outside the walls; Zhang and Supervising Secretary Guang Shiheng defended the Fucheng Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guozhen, the Duke of Xiangcheng, sent fifty thousand troops to camp outside the walls; Zhang and Supervising Secretary Guang Shiheng held the Fucheng Gate.

sentences.zh: 城內外堞凡十五萬四千有奇，三堞一卒。

translations.literal: Battlements inside and outside the wall totaled a little over one hundred fifty-four thousand, with one soldier for every three crenels.
translations.idiomatic: There were some 154,000 crenels inside and outside the walls—one soldier for every three.

sentences.zh: 三月初登陴，閱十日始一還邸，櫛沐易新衣冠。

translations.literal: On the third of the month he first mounted the ramparts; only after ten days did he return once to his residence to wash, comb, and change into fresh robes and hat.
translations.idiomatic: On the third he took the wall; only after ten days did he return home once to bathe and change into clean clothes.

sentences.zh: 家人大駭，章不應。

translations.literal: His household was greatly alarmed; Zhang did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: His family was horrified; he gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 賊傅城下，章手發二炮，賊少卻。

translations.literal: When bandits pressed against the base of the wall, Zhang personally fired two cannon, and the bandits retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels pressed the wall Zhang fired two guns himself and they fell back a little.

sentences.zh: 頃之，各門炮聲絕。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward the cannon at every gate fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long cannon fire at every gate ceased.

sentences.zh: 時亨攝章走，章厲聲曰：「事至此，猶惜死耶！」

translations.literal: Shiheng seized Zhang and tried to flee; Zhang said sternly: "Things have come to this—do you still cling to life?
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng grabbed Zhang to run. Zhang cried out, "It has come to this—and you still want to live?

sentences.zh: 時亨曰：「死此與士卒何別？

translations.literal: Shiheng said: "If we die here, how are we different from the rank and file?
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng said, "If we die here we are no different from common soldiers.

sentences.zh: 入朝訪上所在，不獲則死，死未晚也。」

translations.literal: Enter court and seek where the emperor is; if we cannot find him, then die—death is not yet too late.
translations.idiomatic: Let us go to court and find the emperor; if we cannot, then we die. It is not too late.

sentences.zh: 章從之，與時亨並馬行。

translations.literal: Zhang followed him, and the two rode together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang agreed, and they rode side by side.

sentences.zh: 俄賊突至，呼下馬。

translations.literal: Suddenly bandits burst upon them and shouted for them to dismount.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly rebels rushed up and ordered them down from their horses.

sentences.zh: 時亨倉皇下馬跪，章持鞭不顧，叱曰：「吾視軍御史也，誰敢犯！」

translations.literal: Shiheng hastily dismounted and knelt; Zhang, whip in hand, paid no heed and shouted: "I am the touring army censor—who dares molest me!
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng scrambled off his horse and knelt. Zhang, whip in hand, ignored them and shouted, "I am the army-inspecting censor—who dares touch me!

sentences.zh: 賊刺章股，墮。

translations.literal: Bandits stabbed Zhang in the thigh and he fell.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel stabbed him in the thigh and he fell.

sentences.zh: 章罵曰：「逆賊！

translations.literal: Zhang cursed: "Traitorous bandits!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang cursed, "Traitors!

sentences.zh: 勤王兵且至。

translations.literal: Relief armies loyal to the throne are about to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The relief armies are coming!

sentences.zh: 我死，爾滅不旋踵矣。」

translations.literal: When I die, your destruction will not wait for long.
translations.idiomatic: When I am dead your end will come in no time.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，攢槊刺殺章而去。
