translations.literal: The bandits were furious, thrust with spears in a crowd, killed Zhang, and went away.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they piled on with spears, killed Zhang, and left.

sentences.zh: 抵暮，家人覓屍，猶一手據地坐，張口怒目，勃勃如叱賊狀。

translations.literal: By dusk his family sought his corpse; he still sat with one hand pressing the ground, mouth open and eyes glaring, vigorous as if still berating bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk his family found his body still sitting with one hand on the ground, mouth open and eyes wide, fierce as though still cursing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 妻姜在籍，聞之，一慟而絕。

translations.literal: His wife Jiang was at home on the register; hearing the news, she grieved once and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Jiang was back in their home district; when she heard, she wailed once and died.

sentences.zh: 贈大理寺卿，謚忠烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review with the posthumous title Zhong Lie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review with the temple name Zhong Lie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚節湣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Jie Min.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Jie Min.

sentences.zh: 次子之栻仕閩為職方主事，亦死難。

translations.literal: His second son Zhishi served in Fujian as principal clerk in the Bureau of Military Personnel and also died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zhishi served in Fujian as principal clerk in the Bureau of Military Appointments and also died in the crisis.

sentences.zh: 陳良謨，字士亮，鄞人。

translations.literal: Chen Liangmo, courtesy name Shiliang, was a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Liangmo, styled Shiliang, came from Yin.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士，授大理推官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed investigating officer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Chongzhen, he was appointed investigating officer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 初名天工。

translations.literal: His original name was Tiangong.
translations.idiomatic: His original given name was Tiangong.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝虔事上帝，詔群臣名「天」者悉改之，乃改良謨。

translations.literal: The Chonglie Emperor devoutly served the Supreme Lord; he edicted that all among the ministers whose names contained "Heaven" should change them, whereupon he changed to Liangmo.
translations.idiomatic: The Chonglie Emperor was devoted to the Jade Emperor and ordered all officials whose names contained tian to change them; he took the name Liangmo.

sentences.zh: 在職六年，兩註上考。

translations.literal: In six years in office he twice received top merit evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: In six years on the job he twice earned the highest ratings.

sentences.zh: 行取陛見，擢御史。

translations.literal: Selected by special promotion he was granted audience at court and elevated to censor.
translations.idiomatic: Selected for promotion he was presented at court and made a censor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，出按四川。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was sent out to tour Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was dispatched to inspect Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 期滿當代，再留任。

translations.literal: When his term expired another should have replaced him, but he was kept in office for a second term.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was kept on for another.

sentences.zh: 時流寇大入蜀，詔良謨專護蜀王，巡撫邵捷春專辦賊。

translations.literal: At the time roving bandits penetrated deeply into Shu; an edict ordered Liangmo to devote himself to protecting the Prince of Shu, while Grand Coordinator Shao Jiechun was to focus entirely on the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When bandit armies poured into Sichuan, the court ordered Liangmo to protect the Prince of Shu while Grand Coordinator Shao Jiechun focused on fighting the rebels.

sentences.zh: 良謨飭守具，堅壁清野。

translations.literal: Liangmo readied defensive equipment and enforced walls-held and countryside cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Liangmo prepared defenses and enforced scorched-earth tactics behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 賊犯成都，遣將據要害為掎角。

translations.literal: When bandits assaulted Chengdu, he dispatched generals to hold key points as pincer horns.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels attacked Chengdu he sent generals to hold strategic points in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 一再戰，賊潰奔。

translations.literal: After one or two battles the bandits broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: After several battles the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 帝聞賊擾蜀，下詔責良謨，已聞其善守禦，乃優旨賜銀幣。

translations.literal: The emperor heard bandits were troubling Shu and issued an edict rebuking Liangmo; when he then heard of his skill at defense, he granted silver and coins with a gracious rescript.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of trouble in Sichuan the emperor rebuked Liangmo, but when he learned how well he had defended the province he sent silver and silk with a complimentary edict.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，賊勢益迫，所規畫率不行，而京師陷矣。

translations.literal: When he returned to court the bandit strength grew more pressing; his plans were mostly not carried out, and the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to the capital the rebel threat had grown worse; little of what he proposed was adopted—and then Beijing fell.

sentences.zh: 良謨嘗夢拜文文山於堂下，文山揖之上：「公與予先後一揆，何下拜為？」

translations.literal: Liangmo once dreamed that below the hall he bowed to Wen Tianxiang; Wen Tianxiang bowed him upward, saying: "You and I are of one measure in different times—why bow down?
translations.idiomatic: Liangmo once dreamed he was bowing to Wen Tianxiang below the hall. Wen raised him up: "You and I are alike in different ages—why bow?

sentences.zh: 覺而異之。

translations.literal: Waking, he thought it strange.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he thought it strange.

sentences.zh: 及是城陷，良謨方移疾臥邸中，一慟幾絕，自是水漿不入口。

translations.literal: When the city fell on this occasion, Liangmo was then lying ill at his lodge, grieving once nearly unto death, and from then on would not take even water or broth.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell Liangmo was ill in his quarters. He nearly died of grief and after that refused even water.

sentences.zh: 或勸良謨無死，不答。

translations.literal: Some urged Liangmo not to die; he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him not to die; he made no reply.

sentences.zh: 謂邑子李天葆曰：「吾為國死，義不顧家。

translations.literal: He said to fellow townsman Li Tianbao: "I die for the state; in righteousness I do not look to my family.
translations.idiomatic: He told his townsman Li Tianbao, "I die for the realm and in duty cannot think of my family.

sentences.zh: 惟是母老，先君莫葬，繼嗣未定，須一言耳。」

translations.literal: Only that my mother is old, my late father lies unburied, and the succession is unsettled—this needs a word.
translations.idiomatic: Only that my mother is old, my father unburied, and no heir is fixed—that must be spoken of.

sentences.zh: 因賦詩付天葆。

translations.literal: Thereupon he composed a poem and entrusted it to Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a poem and gave it to Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聞帝崩煤山，大慟曰：「主上不冕服，臣子敢具冠帶乎！

translations.literal: Before long he heard the emperor had perished on Coal Hill and wailed greatly: "If our lord is not in full court dress with crown, how dare ministers properly wear cap and belt!
translations.idiomatic: Soon he heard the emperor had died on Coal Hill and lamented, "The sovereign died without his full regalia—how dare a minister dress in formal cap and belt!

sentences.zh: 吾巾褻，安所得明巾。」

translations.literal: I have only my undercap and everyday garments—where am I to get a proper cap?
translations.idiomatic: I have only my under-clothes—where will I find a proper headcloth?

sentences.zh: 天葆以巾進。

translations.literal: Tianbao presented a cap.
translations.idiomatic: Tianbao offered him a headcloth.

sentences.zh: 良謨著巾，藍便服，起入戶。

translations.literal: Liangmo put on the cap and blue everyday robes, rose, and went into the inner room.
translations.idiomatic: Liangmo put on the cloth, dressed in plain blue, and went inside.

sentences.zh: 妾時氏隨之，遂與妾俱自縊死。

translations.literal: His concubine Lady Shi followed him, and they hanged themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: His concubine Lady Shi followed; together they hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 時氏，京師人，年十八。

translations.literal: Lady Shi was a native of the capital, eighteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shi was from the capital, eighteen years old.

sentences.zh: 良謨逾五十無子，以禮納之，侍良謨百三日耳。

translations.literal: Liangmo was past fifty and without a son; he received her according to ritual, and she had attended Liangmo only a hundred three days.
translations.idiomatic: Liangmo was past fifty without an heir and took her in proper ritual form; she had served him only a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 良謨既卒，其族人以其兄之子久樞為之後。

translations.literal: After Liangmo died his clan set up his elder brother's son Jiushu as his heir.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his clan made his elder brother's son Jiushu his heir.

sentences.zh: 未幾，久樞亦卒，良謨竟無後。

translations.literal: Before long Jiushu also died, and in the end Liangmo had no descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jiushu soon died too, and in the end Liangmo left no line.

sentences.zh: 贈太仆卿，謚恭湣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with the posthumous title Gong Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made chief minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud with the temple name Gong Min.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚恭潔。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Gong Jie.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Gong Jie.

sentences.zh: 陳純德，字靜生，零陵人。

translations.literal: Chen Chunde, courtesy name Jingsheng, was a native of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Chunde, styled Jingsheng, came from Lingling.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，以學行稱。

translations.literal: As a student he was renowned for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As a student he was known for learning and character.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜泊洞庭，為盜窘，躍出墮水，再躍入洲渚。

translations.literal: Once he moored at night on Dongting Lake, was pressed by bandits, leaped out and fell into the water, then leaped again onto a sandbank.
translations.idiomatic: Once he anchored on Dongting at night; robbed, he leapt overboard, fell into the water, then sprang onto a sandbar.

sentences.zh: 比曉，坐蘆葦中，去泊舟數十丈。

translations.literal: By dawn he sat among the reeds, several tens of paces from where the boat was moored.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn he sat among the reeds, dozens of yards from where his boat lay.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十三年成進士，年已六十矣。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the metropolitan examination; he was already sixty years old.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen, by which time he was already sixty.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝召諸進士，咨以時事。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuanglie summoned the new jinshi and consulted them on current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor summoned the new graduates and asked their views on affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 純德奏稱旨，立擢御史，巡按山西。

translations.literal: Chunde's memorial pleased the throne; he was immediately promoted to censor and sent to inspect Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chunde's answers pleased the emperor, who at once named him censor and assigned him to inspect Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 七月，部內嚴霜，民凍餒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month severe frost fell within his jurisdiction; the people suffered cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month hard frost struck his circuit, and the people froze and starved.

sentences.zh: 純德上疏請恤，因陳抽練之弊，言：「兵抽則人失故居，無父母妻子之依，田園丘壟之戀，思歸則逃，逢敵則潰。

translations.literal: Chunde memorialized requesting relief, and also set forth the abuses of selective extraction and training, saying: "When troops are extracted, men lose their old homes, lacking parents, wives, and children to rely on and longing for field and grave; they flee if they think of return, and break if they meet the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Chunde petitioned for relief and exposed the evils of the selective-training system, writing: "When soldiers are skimmed from local units, they lose their homes—cut off from parents, wives, and children, from fields and family graves. They desert when they yearn for home and rout at the first clash.

sentences.zh: 抽余者即以餉薄而安於無用，抽去者又以遠調而不樂為用。

translations.literal: Those left behind, because pay is thin, are content to be useless; those extracted are transferred far away and are unwilling to serve.
translations.idiomatic: The men left behind make do with meager pay and see no duty in being useful; those taken away resist distant postings and serve unwillingly.

sentences.zh: 伍虛而餉仍在，不歸主帥，則歸偏裨，樂其逃而利其餉，凡藉以營求遷秩，皆是物也。

translations.literal: Squads are empty yet pay still flows; if it does not go to the commander-in-chief, it goes to subordinate officers. They welcome desertions and profit from the pay; all who exploit this to seek promotion through intrigue are such creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Companies stand empty while rations still flow—not to the commanding general but to junior officers who profit from desertion and hoard the pay. Everyone who schemes promotion through such fraud is of this breed.

sentences.zh: 精神不以束伍，而以侵餉；

translations.literal: Their energy goes not to holding the ranks together but to embezzling pay;
translations.idiomatic: Their zeal goes not into keeping ranks full but into stealing rations;

sentences.zh: 厚餉不以養士，而以求官。

translations.literal: Generous pay is not used to support soldiers but to buy office.
translations.idiomatic: Fat allowances are not spent on the troops but on buying advancement.

sentences.zh: 伍虛則無人，安望其練；

translations.literal: If squads are empty there are no men—how can one expect drilling?
translations.idiomatic: Empty companies mean no men to drill—how can training succeed?

sentences.zh: 餉糜則愈缺，安望其充。

translations.literal: If pay is wasted it becomes ever more lacking—how can one expect full ranks?
translations.idiomatic: When pay is squandered the coffers run dry—how can companies ever be filled?

sentences.zh: 此今日行間大弊也。」

translations.literal: These are the great abuses in the armies today."
translations.idiomatic: This is the chief disease crippling the armies today.

sentences.zh: 帝不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor could not adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 還朝，督畿輔學政。

translations.literal: On returning to court he supervised education policy in the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he oversaw education in the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 將出按部，都城陷。

translations.literal: As he was about to go out on inspection tour, the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: He was preparing to set out on circuit when the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 賊下令百官以某日入見，眾攝純德入，還邸慟哭，遂自經。

translations.literal: The bandits ordered all officials to present themselves on a certain day. The crowd seized Chunde and brought him in. He returned to his lodging, wept bitterly, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels ordered officials to appear on a set day. Others dragged Chunde along, but once home he went to his quarters, wept, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 京山人秦嘉系買地葬之永定門外，立石表墓焉。

translations.literal: Qin Jiaxi of Jingshan bought land and buried him outside Yongding Gate, erecting a stone tablet at the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jiaxi of Jingshan purchased a plot outside Yongding Gate and buried him there, with a stone marker at the grave.

sentences.zh: 贈太仆卿，謚恭節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grand Master of the Stud, with posthumous title Gongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously promoted to Grand Master of the Stud and given the posthumous title Gongjie ("Reverent Integrity").

sentences.zh: 申佳允，字孔嘉。

translations.literal: Shen Jiayun, courtesy name Kongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiayun, styled Kongjia.

sentences.zh: 永年人。

translations.literal: He was a native of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: He came from Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 授儀封知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 縣故多盜，佳允嚴保甲法，盜無所容。

translations.literal: The county had long been full of bandits; Jiayun strictly enforced the baojia system, and bandits had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: The county had long been infested with bandits; Jiayun enforced the baojia household-defense system so strictly that thieves could find no refuge.

sentences.zh: 霪雨河決，艤舟怒濤中，塞其口。

translations.literal: In incessant rain the river burst its banks; he moored a boat in the raging torrent and blocked the breach.
translations.idiomatic: When weeks of rain burst the river, he anchored a boat in the flood and plugged the break from it.

sentences.zh: 捕大猾置之法。

translations.literal: He captured a great rascal and punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: He seized a notorious outlaw and had him punished to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 以才調杞縣。

translations.literal: For his talent he was transferred to Qixian.
translations.idiomatic: His ability won him a transfer to Qixian.

sentences.zh: 八年，賊掃地王率萬人來攻，城土垣多圮。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the bandit Saodiwang led ten thousand men to attack; the earthen walls were largely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the rebel Saodiwang marched ten thousand men against the city; its earthen ramparts were crumbling.

sentences.zh: 佳允募死士擊走賊，因甓其城。

translations.literal: Jiayun recruited dare-to-die men, drove off the bandits, and then faced the walls with brick.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun raised a corps of volunteers, beat the rebels back, and rebuilt the walls in brick.

sentences.zh: 唐王聿鍵勤王，將抵開封。

translations.literal: Prince Tang Yujian was coming to aid the throne and was about to reach Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tang Zhu Yujian was marching to the emperor's relief and was nearing Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 諸大吏惴恐，集議曰：「留之，不聽。

translations.literal: The high officials were fearful and convened in counsel, saying: "If we keep him, he will not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified senior officials met and said, "If we detain him, he will not listen.

sentences.zh: 行，守土者且得罪。」

translations.literal: If we let him go, those who hold the soil will yet be blamed."
translations.idiomatic: If we let him pass, the local defenders will be punished.

sentences.zh: 佳允曰：「惟周王可留之。」

translations.literal: Jiayun said: "Only the Prince of Zhou can detain him."
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun said, "Only the Prince of Zhou can hold him."

sentences.zh: 眾稱善，用其計。

translations.literal: All praised the plan and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly approved, and they followed his plan.

sentences.zh: 治行卓異，擢吏部文選主事，上備邊五策。

translations.literal: His administration was outstanding; he was promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Appointments Section and submitted five policies for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: Marked out for exceptional service, he was raised to principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's appointments office and presented five proposals for securing the borders.

sentences.zh: 進考功員外郎，佐京察。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice director in the Bureau of Merit Evaluation and assisted in the capital-wide personnel review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Merit Evaluation and helped conduct the capital-wide personnel review.

sentences.zh: 大學士薛國觀傾少詹事文安之。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan persecuted Junior Guardian Wen Anzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xue Guoguan moved to ruin Junior Guardian Wen Anzhi.

sentences.zh: 安之，佳允座主也，事連佳允，左遷南京國子博士。

translations.literal: Anzhi was Jiayun's examination patron; the affair implicated Jiayun, who was demoted to doctor of the Nanjing National University.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhi had been Jiayun's patron in the examinations; the case dragged Jiayun down, and he was demoted to lecturer at the Nanjing National University.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷大理評事，進太仆丞，閱馬近畿。

translations.literal: After a long while he was moved to reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review, then advanced to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and inspected horses in the metropolitan region.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he became a reviewing officer in the Court of Judicial Review, then vice director of the Imperial Stud, inspecting horses around the capital.

sentences.zh: 聞李自成破居庸，嘆曰：「京師不守矣！

translations.literal: Hearing that Li Zicheng had broken through Juyong Pass, he sighed and said: "The capital cannot be held!
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Li Zicheng had taken Juyong Pass, he sighed, "The capital is lost!

sentences.zh: 君父有難，焉逃死？」

translations.literal: The sovereign and father are in peril—how can one flee and save one's life?"
translations.idiomatic: Our lord and father are in peril—how can I run and live?

sentences.zh: 馳入都，遍謁大臣為畫戰守策，皆不省。

translations.literal: He galloped into the capital, visited every great minister to lay out plans for war and defense, and none paid heed.
translations.idiomatic: He raced into the city, called on every senior minister with plans for defense, and none would listen.

sentences.zh: 貽子涵光書曰：「行己曰義，順數曰命；

translations.literal: He wrote to his son Zihanguang, saying: "To conduct oneself is called righteousness; to follow one's allotted span is called fate;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his son Zihanguang: "To live rightly is righteousness; to accept what heaven ordains is fate.

sentences.zh: 義不可背也，命不可違也。

translations.literal: righteousness cannot be betrayed, and fate cannot be defied.
translations.idiomatic: Righteousness must not be betrayed, and fate must not be defied.

sentences.zh: 天下事莫不壞於貪生而畏死。

translations.literal: Nothing under heaven is ruined more than clinging to life out of greed and fearing death.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing under heaven comes to ruin faster than clinging to life and fearing death.

sentences.zh: 死於疾，死於利，死於刑戮，於房幃，於鬥戰，均死也，死數者不死君父，蓋亦不善用死矣。

translations.literal: To die of illness, die for profit, die by execution, die in the bedchamber, die in battle—all are death alike; those who die in such numbers do not die for sovereign and father, and so they do not know how to use death well either.
translations.idiomatic: Death from sickness, from gain, from the executioner's blade, in the bedchamber, or on the battlefield is still death—but those who die in such ways do not die for their lord and father, and so they do not know how to die well.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，君父之事，死義也，猶命也，我則行之。」

translations.literal: Today's affair is the affair of lord and father; to die for righteousness is likewise fate—and I shall carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: What faces us today is the affair of lord and father; to die for righteousness is also fate, and I mean to do it.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，冠帶辭母，策馬至王恭廠，從者請易服以避賊。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he put on cap and sash to take leave of his mother, spurred his horse to Wanggongchang, and his attendants asked him to change clothes to avoid the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he dressed in full official regalia to bid his mother farewell, then rode to Wanggongchang. His servants begged him to change clothes to escape the rebels.

sentences.zh: 佳允曰：「吾起微賤，食祿十三年。

translations.literal: Jiayun said: "I rose from humble origins and have eaten salary for thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun said, "I came from nothing and have drawn the state's pay for thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 國事至此，敢愛死乎！」

translations.literal: The state's affairs have come to this—how dare I cherish my life!"
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in this pass—how dare I cling to life!

sentences.zh: 兩仆環守不去，紿之曰：「吾不死也，我將擇善地焉。」

translations.literal: Two servants surrounded him and would not leave; he deceived them, saying: "I will not die; I am going to choose a fitting place."
translations.idiomatic: Two servants held close and would not leave. He lied: "I am not going to die—I am only choosing a proper place."

sentences.zh: 下馬，旁見灌畦巨井，急躍入。

translations.literal: He dismounted, saw beside him a great well in an irrigated field, and leaped in at once.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, spotted a great well beside the irrigated plots, and threw himself in.

sentences.zh: 仆號呼，欲出之。

translations.literal: The servants cried out and tried to pull him out.
translations.idiomatic: They screamed and tried to haul him out.

sentences.zh: 佳允亦呼曰：「告太安人，有子作忠臣，勿過傷也。」

translations.literal: Jiayun also cried: "Tell Madame Tai'an that she has a son who became a loyal minister—do not grieve too much."
translations.idiomatic: Jiayun called back, "Tell my mother that she has a son who died a loyal minister—grieve no more than you must.

sentences.zh: 遂死，年四十二，贈太仆少卿，謚節湣。

translations.literal: Thus he died, aged forty-two. He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, with posthumous title Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned at forty-two. He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Stud and given the posthumous title Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚端湣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Duanmin.

sentences.zh: 成德，字元升，霍州人，依舅氏占籍懷柔。

translations.literal: Cheng De, courtesy name Yuansheng, was a native of Huozhou; relying on his mother's clan he registered his household in Huairou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng De, styled Yuansheng, came from Huozhou but was registered in Huairou through his uncle's household.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fourth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 除滋陽知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Ziyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Ziyang.

sentences.zh: 性剛介，清操絕俗，疾惡若仇。

translations.literal: By nature he was stern and upright, his integrity beyond the common run, hating evil as if it were a personal enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Fiercely upright, he held himself to a purity few could match and hated wrongdoing as he would a sworn foe.

sentences.zh: 文震孟入都，德郊迎，執弟子禮，語刺溫體仁，體仁聞而恨之。

translations.literal: When Wen Zhenmeng entered the capital, De went out to the suburbs to welcome him, performed the rites of a disciple, and in conversation attacked Wen Tiren; Tiren heard and hated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhenmeng reached the capital, De rode out to meet him, treated him as his teacher, and in conversation lashed Wen Tiren—who took note and bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 兗州知府增餉額，德固爭，又嘗捕治其牙爪吏。

translations.literal: The prefect of Yanzhou increased the levy quota; De firmly opposed it and had once arrested and punished one of his henchman clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanzhou prefect raised the tax quota; De fought him stubbornly and once had one of his bully clerks arrested and punished.

sentences.zh: 知府怒，讒於御史禹好善。

translations.literal: The prefect was angry and slandered him to Censor Yu Haoshan.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect, furious, denounced him to Censor Yu Haoshan.

sentences.zh: 好善，體仁客也，誣德貪虐，逮入京。

translations.literal: Haoshan was Tiren's client; he falsely accused De of greed and cruelty and had him seized and brought to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Haoshan was Tiren's man; he charged De with corruption and cruelty and had him hauled to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 滋陽民詣闕訟冤。

translations.literal: The people of Ziyang went to the palace gates to plead his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ziyang marched to the palace gates to protest his innocence.

sentences.zh: 震孟在閣，亦為之稱枉。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng was in the Grand Secretariat and also spoke on his behalf that he had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng, now in the Grand Secretariat, also declared the case unjust.

sentences.zh: 德道中具疏極論體仁罪，而震孟已被體仁擠而去之。

translations.literal: On the road De prepared a memorial in full setting forth Tiren's crimes, but Zhenmeng had already been driven out by Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: On the road De drafted a memorial detailing Tiren's crimes—but Zhenmeng had already been forced from office by him.

sentences.zh: 好善再劾德，言其疏出震孟手，帝不之究。

translations.literal: Haoshan impeached De again, saying the memorial had come from Zhenmeng's hand; the emperor did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Haoshan impeached De again, claiming the memorial was Zhenmeng's work; the emperor let it drop.

sentences.zh: 德母張伺體仁長安街，繞輿大罵，拾瓦礫擲之。

translations.literal: De's mother Zhang waited for Tiren on Chang'an Avenue, circled his carriage cursing loudly, and picked up tiles and stones to throw at him.
translations.idiomatic: De's mother, née Zhang, ambushed Tiren on Chang'an Avenue, circled his carriage shouting abuse, and pelted him with rubble.

sentences.zh: 體仁恚，疏聞於朝。

translations.literal: Tiren was enraged and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren, furious, reported the incident to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔五城御史驅逐，移德鎮撫獄掠治。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Five-City censors to drive her off; De was transferred to the Brocade Guard prison for torture and interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the metropolitan censors to remove her and had De thrown into the Brocade Guard prison for torture.

sentences.zh: 杖六十午門外，戍邊。

translations.literal: He was beaten sixty strokes outside the Meridian Gate and banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was flogged sixty strokes outside the Meridian Gate and sent into frontier exile.

sentences.zh: 坐贓六千有奇。

translations.literal: He was convicted of embezzlement exceeding six thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He was convicted on a charge of embezzling more than six thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 而給體仁校尉五十人護出入。

translations.literal: Yet fifty guard officers were given to Tiren to escort him in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fifty imperial guards were assigned to escort Tiren wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 德居戍所七年，用御史詹兆恒薦，起如臯知縣。

translations.literal: De lived at his place of exile for seven years; on the recommendation of Censor Zhan Zhaoheng he was recalled as magistrate of Rugao.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years in exile, Censor Zhan Zhaoheng's recommendation brought him back as magistrate of Rugao.

sentences.zh: 尋擢武庫主事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to principal clerk in the Armory Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to principal clerk in the Armory Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以母老辭，不允，乃就道。

translations.literal: He pleaded that his mother was old; permission was denied, and he took to the road.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to stay home because his mother was elderly; the court refused, and he set out for the capital.

sentences.zh: 至則上言：「年來中外多故，居官者爵祿迷心，廉恥道喪。

translations.literal: On arrival he memorialized: "In recent years troubles have multiplied within and without; those in office are bewitched by rank and salary, and the way of integrity and shame is lost.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he memorialized: "In these years turmoil has multiplied at home and abroad. Officials are dazzled by rank and pay; integrity and shame have vanished.

sentences.zh: 陛下禦極十七年，何仗節死義之寥寥也！

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ruled for seventeen years—how few are those who hold the tally and die for righteousness!
translations.idiomatic: In seventeen years on the throne, how few men have held to their principles and died for the cause!

sentences.zh: 宋臣張栻有言：『仗節死義之臣，當於犯顏諫諍中求之。』

translations.literal: The Song minister Zhang Shi said: 'Ministers who hold the tally and die for righteousness are to be sought among those who offend the countenance and remonstrate.'
translations.idiomatic: The Song scholar Zhang Shi wrote: 'Men who die holding their principles are found among those who speak truth to power.'

sentences.zh: 夫犯顏諫諍何難，在朝廷養之而已。

translations.literal: To offend the countenance and remonstrate is not hard—it depends only on the court nurturing such men.
translations.idiomatic: To speak boldly is not hard in itself; what matters is that the court nurture such men.

sentences.zh: 表厥宅裏，所以伸忠臣孝子於生前；

translations.literal: To mark out the dwelling and lane is to extend loyal ministers and filial sons while they still live;
translations.idiomatic: Honor a man's house and lane while he lives, and loyal ministers and filial sons will flourish;

sentences.zh: 殊厥井疆，所以誅亂臣賊子於未死。

translations.literal: to set apart the well and field boundaries is to punish rebellious ministers and wicked sons before they die.
translations.idiomatic: strip the lands of traitors before they die, and rebels and parricides will fear to act.

sentences.zh: 茍死敵者無功，則媚敵者且無罪；

translations.literal: If those who die fighting the enemy receive no merit, then those who fawn on the enemy will yet go unpunished;
translations.idiomatic: If men who die fighting the enemy win no reward, those who bow to the enemy will go unpunished;

sentences.zh: 死賊者褒揚不亟，則從賊者恬而不知畏也。」

translations.literal: if those who die resisting bandits are not swiftly praised and exalted, then those who follow bandits will be at ease and know no fear."
translations.idiomatic: if those who die resisting rebels are not swiftly honored, those who join the rebels will feel safe and unafraid.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城破，不知帝所在，旁皇廳事。

translations.literal: Before long the city fell; not knowing where the emperor was, he wandered distraught in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after, the city fell. Not knowing where the emperor was, he paced the hall in anguish.

sentences.zh: 已，趨至午門，見兵部尚書張縉彥自賊所出。

translations.literal: Presently he hurried to the Meridian Gate and saw Minister of War Zhang Jinyan coming out from the bandits' side.
translations.idiomatic: He rushed to the Meridian Gate and saw Minister of War Zhang Jinyan emerging from the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 德以頭觸縉彥胸，且詈之，俄聞帝崩，痛哭。

translations.literal: De struck Jinyan's chest with his head and cursed him; soon hearing that the emperor had perished, he wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: De butted his head into Jinyan's chest and cursed him; moments later, hearing the emperor was dead, he broke into wailing.

sentences.zh: 持雞酒奔東華門，奠梓宮於茶棚之下，觸地流血。

translations.literal: He took chicken and wine and ran to the East Flowery Gate, offering libation to the imperial coffin beneath a tea shed, his forehead striking the ground until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: He seized offerings of chicken and wine, ran to the East Flowery Gate, and poured libations before the emperor's coffin under a tea-shed, beating his forehead on the ground until it bled.

sentences.zh: 賊露刃脅之，不為動。

translations.literal: Bandits bared blades to threaten him; he was not moved.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels bared their blades at him; he did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 奠畢歸家，有妹年二十余未嫁，德顧之曰：「我死，汝何依？」

translations.literal: When the rites were finished he returned home. He had a younger sister of more than twenty, still unmarried. De looked at her and said: "When I die, whom will you rely on?"
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he went home. His younger sister, over twenty and still unmarried, stood before him. De said, "When I am gone, whom will you have?

sentences.zh: 妹曰：「兄死，妹請前。」

translations.literal: His sister said: "When brother dies, your sister asks to go first."
translations.idiomatic: She answered, "When you die, let your sister go first."

sentences.zh: 德稱善，哭而視其縊。

translations.literal: De praised her, wept, and watched as she hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: He praised her, wept, and stayed while she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 入別其母，哭盡哀，出而自縊。

translations.literal: He went in to take leave of his mother, wept his fill of grief, went out, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to bid his mother farewell, wept until grief was spent, then went out and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 母見子女皆死，亦投繯死。

translations.literal: When the mother saw her children both dead, she too threw a noose and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing both children dead, his mother hanged herself as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，懷柔城破，德父文桂遇害，家屬盡沒。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huairou fell, De's father Wengui was killed and the household was entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Huairou fell, De's father Wengui was killed and the family wiped out.

sentences.zh: 妻劉在京，以征德贓急，憂悸死。

translations.literal: His wife Liu was in the capital; pressed to pay De's alleged embezzlement, she died of anxiety and shock.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Liu, in Beijing, was hounded to pay the fine for his supposed graft and died of grief and terror.

sentences.zh: 至是，又闔門死難，惟幼子先寄友人家獲存。

translations.literal: Now again the whole household died in the calamity; only the youngest son, sent beforehand to a friend's home, survived.
translations.idiomatic: Now the whole household perished; only the youngest son, sent earlier to a friend's house, was spared.

sentences.zh: 贈德光祿卿，謚忠毅。

translations.literal: De was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, with posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: De was posthumously made Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and given the posthumous title Zhongyi ("Loyal and Resolute").

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚介湣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous title Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 許直，字若魯，如臯人。

translations.literal: Xu Zhi, courtesy name Ruolu, was a native of Rugao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhi, styled Ruolu, came from Rugao.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年成進士。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the seventh year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 出文震孟之門，以名節自砥，除義烏知縣。

translations.literal: He came from Wen Zhenmeng's school, sharpened himself on reputation and integrity, and was appointed magistrate of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: A disciple of Wen Zhenmeng, he honed himself on probity and principle and was appointed magistrate of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，哀毀骨立，終喪蔬食，寢柩旁。

translations.literal: He returned home for his mother's mourning; grief wasted him to skin and bone; through the full mourning period he ate only vegetables and slept beside the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went home to mourn; grief left him emaciated; for the full mourning year he ate plain food only and slept beside the bier.

sentences.zh: 補廣東惠來縣。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Huilai County in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was then posted to Huilai County in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 用清望，征授吏部文選主事，進考功員外郎。

translations.literal: On account of his pure reputation he was summoned and appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's Bureau of Appointments, then promoted to vice director in the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: His unstained reputation won him a capital summons: chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel's appointments bureau, then vice director in the evaluations bureau.

sentences.zh: 賊薄都城，約同官出貲饗士，為死守計。

translations.literal: When the rebels closed on the capital, he agreed with his colleagues to pool funds to feast the troops for a plan of desperate defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels pressed the capital, he and his colleagues agreed to contribute funds to feast the soldiers and prepare a last stand.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊令百官報名。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the rebels ordered all officials to register their names.
translations.idiomatic: After the city fell, the rebels ordered every official to report and register.

sentences.zh: 直曰：「身可殺，志不可奪。」

translations.literal: Zhi said: "The body may be killed, but the will cannot be wrested away."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "They may kill my body, but they cannot break my resolve.

sentences.zh: 有傳帝南狩者，直將往從。

translations.literal: When word came that the emperor had gone south on campaign, Zhi prepared to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When rumor spread that the emperor had fled south, Zhi set out to join him.

sentences.zh: 見賊騎塞道，出門輒返，曰：「四方兵戈，駕焉往？

translations.literal: He saw rebel horsemen blocking the roads; each time he went out he turned back and said: "War rages on every side—where can the imperial carriage go?
translations.idiomatic: Rebel cavalry choked the roads; he went out and turned back again and again, saying, "Arms blaze on every side—where can the Son of Heaven's carriage go?

sentences.zh: 國亂不匡，君危無濟，我何生為！」

translations.literal: The realm is in chaos and I cannot set it right; the sovereign is in peril and I cannot save him—what is left for me to live for!"
translations.idiomatic: The state is in turmoil and I cannot rescue it; the ruler is in danger and I cannot save him—why should I go on living!

sentences.zh: 已，知帝崩，一慟幾絕。

translations.literal: When he then learned the emperor was dead, he was overcome with grief nearly to the point of death.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the emperor was dead, his grief was so violent he nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 客以七十老父為解，直曰：「不死，辱及所生。」

translations.literal: A visitor urged him to spare himself for the sake of his father, who was seventy; Zhi said: "If I do not die, I bring shame on those who gave me life."
translations.idiomatic: A friend pleaded that his father was seventy; Zhi said, "If I live on, I disgrace those who bore me.

sentences.zh: 賦絕命詩六章，闔戶自經。

translations.literal: He composed six poems of parting, closed his door, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote six death poems, shut his door, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 越旦視之，神氣如生。

translations.literal: The next morning those who looked upon him found his spirit seemed still alive.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning those who viewed his body said his bearing was as if he still lived.

sentences.zh: 贈太仆卿，謚忠節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and given the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of the Imperial Stud and granted the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠湣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 直有族子德溥者，在南，聞莊烈帝崩，大哭數日。

translations.literal: Zhi had a clansman Debo in the south who, on hearing of Emperor Zhuanglie's death, wept for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi had a kinsman Debo in the south who, when he heard that Emperor Zhuanglie was dead, wept for days on end.

sentences.zh: 揚州陷，又哭數日。

translations.literal: When Yangzhou fell he wept again for many days.
translations.idiomatic: When Yangzhou fell he wept again for days on end.

sentences.zh: 每獨坐輒慟哭，食必以崇禎錢一枚置幾上，祭而後食，食已復哭。

translations.literal: Whenever he sat alone he would sob; before each meal he placed one Chongzhen coin on the table, made an offering, and only then ate—and when he had finished, wept again.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sat alone he broke into tears; before every meal he set a single Chongzhen coin on the table, made a small offering, and only then ate—and wept again when he had finished.

sentences.zh: 又刺其兩臂曰：「生為明臣，死為明鬼。」

translations.literal: He also carved on both arms: "Born a minister of Ming, dead a ghost of Ming."
translations.idiomatic: He also carved into both arms: "Born a minister of the Ming, dead a ghost of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 事發，死西市。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light he was executed at the West Market.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was discovered he was put to death at the West Market.

sentences.zh: 金鉉，字伯玉，武進人，占籍順天之大興。

translations.literal: Jin Xuan, courtesy name Boyu, was a native of Wujin but registered his domicile in Daxing of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Xuan, styled Boyu, came from Wujin but was enrolled as a resident of Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 祖汝升，南京戶部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rusheng had been vice minister in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rusheng had served as vice minister in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 父顯名，汀州知府。

translations.literal: His father Xianming had been prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xianming had been prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 鉉少有大志，以聖賢自期許。

translations.literal: Even as a youth Xuan cherished great resolve and measured himself against the sages.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Xuan set his heart on great things and took the sages as his standard.

sentences.zh: 年十八舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At eighteen he came first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，崇禎改元，成進士。

translations.literal: The next year, when the reign name changed to Chongzhen, he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the inaugural year of Chongzhen, he passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 不習為吏，改揚州府教授，日訓諸生闡濂、洛正學。

translations.literal: Unwilling to mold himself into a routine bureaucrat, he was transferred to instructor at Yangzhou Prefecture and daily instructed the students in the orthodox learning of the Lian and Luo schools.
translations.idiomatic: He had no taste for routine office work and was made prefectural instructor at Yangzhou, where each day he led his students in the orthodox teachings of the Zhou and Cheng schools.

sentences.zh: 燕居言動，俱有規格，諸生嚴憚之。

translations.literal: In daily life his words and bearing were all governed by rule; the students stood in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: In private as in public his speech and conduct were measured; the students held him in deep awe.

sentences.zh: 歷國子博士、工部主事。

translations.literal: He served in succession as lecturer in the Imperial Academy and principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to lecturer in the Imperial Academy and principal clerk in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝方銳意綜核，疑廷臣朋黨營私。

translations.literal: The emperor was then keen to scrutinize everything, suspecting court ministers of faction and self-interest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then intent on tightening control, suspecting that court ministers formed factions and pursued private gain.

sentences.zh: 度支告匱，四方亟用兵，餉不敷，遣中官張彜憲總理戶、工二部，建專署，檄諸曹謁見，禮視堂官。

translations.literal: The revenue board reported empty coffers; troops were urgently needed on every front and pay could not be met; eunuch Zhang Yixian was sent to superintend both the Ministries of Revenue and Works, established a separate office, and issued orders to every bureau that they should present themselves to him with the courtesies due a department chief.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury was empty; war pressed on every side and pay could not be met; the eunuch Zhang Yixian was dispatched to oversee both the Revenue and Works ministries, set up his own office, and ordered every bureau to attend on him with the ceremony owed a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 鉉恥之，再疏爭，不納。

translations.literal: Xuan was ashamed of this and memorialized twice in protest; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was shamed by this and memorialized twice in protest, but his pleas were ignored.

sentences.zh: 乃約兩部諸僚，私謁者眾唾其面，彜憲慍甚。

translations.literal: He then agreed with colleagues in both ministries that whoever made a private call on Zhang should be spat upon in the face; Zhang was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined colleagues in both ministries in a pact: whoever paid Zhang a private visit would be spat in the face by the rest; Zhang was furious.

sentences.zh: 鉉當榷稅杭州，辭疾請假。

translations.literal: When it was Xuan's turn to supervise the commodity tax at Hangzhou, he pleaded illness and asked for leave.
translations.idiomatic: When his turn came to supervise the commodity levy at Hangzhou, he pleaded illness and sought leave.

sentences.zh: 彜憲摭火器不中程，劾鉉落職。

translations.literal: Zhang seized on ordnance that failed to meet specifications and impeached Xuan, stripping him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang seized on firearms that failed inspection and impeached Xuan, who was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 鉉杜門謝客，躬爨以養父母。

translations.literal: Xuan shut his doors to visitors and personally cooked to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan closed his doors to guests and cooked for his parents himself.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，始起兵部主事，巡視皇城。

translations.literal: In spring of the seventeenth year he was at last restored as principal clerk in the Ministry of War and charged with inspecting the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year he was at last recalled as principal clerk in the Ministry of War and assigned to inspect the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 聞大同陷，疏曰：「宣、大，京師北門。

translations.literal: When he heard Datong had fallen he memorialized: "Xuanfu and Datong are the northern gates of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Datong had fallen, he memorialized: "Xuanfu and Datong are the capital's northern gates.

sentences.zh: 大同陷則宣府危，宣府危，大事去矣。

translations.literal: If Datong falls Xuanfu is endangered; if Xuanfu is endangered, the great cause is lost.
translations.idiomatic: If Datong falls, Xuanfu is in peril; if Xuanfu is in peril, the dynasty is lost.

sentences.zh: 請急撤回監宣中官杜勛，專任巡撫朱之馮。

translations.literal: I beg that the supervising eunuch Du Xun at Xuanfu be urgently recalled and full authority vested in the grand coordinator Zhu Zhifeng.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the eunuch inspector Du Xun at Xuanfu be recalled at once and full authority given to Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhifeng.

sentences.zh: 勛二心僨事，之馮忠懇，可屬大事。」

translations.literal: Du is of divided loyalty and has ruined affairs; Zhu is loyal and earnest—great matters may be entrusted to him."
translations.idiomatic: Du is double-hearted and has botched the defense; Zhu is loyal and sincere—he can be trusted with the crisis.

sentences.zh: 不報，未幾，勛以宣府下賊，賊殺之馮，烽火逼京師。

translations.literal: No reply came; before long Du surrendered Xuanfu to the rebels, who killed Zhu; beacon fires pressed on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: No answer came. Soon Du handed Xuanfu to the rebels; they killed Zhu, and alarm fires closed on the capital.

sentences.zh: 鉉奔告母：「母可且逃匿。

translations.literal: Xuan rushed to tell his mother: "Mother, you may go into hiding for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan ran to his mother and said, "Mother, you should hide for now.

sentences.zh: 兒受國恩，義當死。」

translations.literal: Your son has received the state's grace and by right should die."
translations.idiomatic: Your son has received the state's favor and ought to die for it.

sentences.zh: 鉉母章時年八十余矣，呵曰：「爾受國恩，我不受國恩乎！

translations.literal: Xuan's mother Zhang was already more than eighty; she rebuked him: "You have received the state's grace—have I not received the state's grace!
translations.idiomatic: His mother Zhang was already past eighty. She scolded him: "You have received the state's grace—have I not received the state's grace!

sentences.zh: 廡下井，是我死所也。」

translations.literal: The well under the corridor is where I shall die."
translations.idiomatic: The well beneath the side hall is where I die."

sentences.zh: 鉉哭而去。

translations.literal: Xuan wept and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan wept and went away.

sentences.zh: 城破，趨入朝，宮人紛紛出。

translations.literal: When the city was broken he hurried to the court; palace women were streaming out in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the walls were breached he rushed to court; palace women poured out in confusion.

sentences.zh: 知帝已崩，解牙牌拜授家人，即投金水河。

translations.literal: Learning the emperor was already dead, he removed his tally of office, bowed and handed it to his household, and cast himself into the Golden Water River.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the emperor was already dead, he took off his ivory tally, bowed and gave it to his family, and threw himself into the Golden Water River.

sentences.zh: 家人爭前挽之，鉉怒，口嚙其臂，得脫，遂躍入水。

translations.literal: His household rushed forward to seize him; in anger he bit an arm that held him, broke free, and leaped into the water.
translations.idiomatic: His servants rushed to pull him back; he bit the arm that held him, broke free, and plunged in.

sentences.zh: 水淺，濡首泥中乃絕。

translations.literal: The water was shallow; with his head drenched in the mud he died.
translations.idiomatic: The water was shallow; his head sank in the mud and he died.

sentences.zh: 母聞即投井，妾王隨之，皆死。

translations.literal: When his mother heard it she at once threw herself into the well; his concubine Wang followed—all died.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother heard, she threw herself into the well at once; his concubine Wang followed—all perished.

sentences.zh: 賊踞大內，逾月始去。

translations.literal: The rebels occupied the inner palace for more than a month before they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the inner palace for more than a month before they left.

sentences.zh: 金水河冠袍泛泛見水上，內官群指之曰：「此金兵部也。」

translations.literal: Caps and robes belonging to Xuan floated on the Golden Water River; the palace eunuchs pointed and said: "That is Vice Minister Jin of the War Ministry."
translations.idiomatic: Official caps and robes floated on the Golden Water River; the palace eunuchs pointed and said, "That is Jin of the War Ministry.

sentences.zh: 弟錝辨其屍，驗網巾環，得鉉首歸，合以木身，如禮而殮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zuan identified the corpse; checking the mesh kerchief ring, he recovered Xuan's head and returned to bury it with a wooden body in full rites.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zuan identified the body; by the mesh kerchief ring he recovered Xuan's head and buried it with a wooden effigy in proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 事竣，錝自經。

translations.literal: When all was done, Zuan hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, Zuan hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 後贈鉉太仆少卿，謚忠節。

translations.literal: Later Xuan was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and given the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud and granted the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 本朝賜謚忠潔。

translations.literal: Our dynasty granted the posthumous name Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: The present dynasty bestowed the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal Purity).

sentences.zh: 右範景文至鉉二十有一人，皆自引決。

translations.literal: From Fan Jingwen to Xuan, twenty-one men in all took their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: From Fan Jingwen down to Jin Xuan, twenty-one men in all chose death by their own hand.

sentences.zh: 其他率委蛇見賊。

translations.literal: The rest generally yielded obsequiously and presented themselves to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The rest for the most part bowed and scraped and went to register with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊以大僚多誤國，概囚縶之。

translations.literal: The rebels, believing that high officials had largely ruined the state, imprisoned them wholesale.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, holding that senior ministers had largely ruined the realm, threw them into prison en masse.

sentences.zh: 庶官則或用或否，用者下吏政府銓除，不用者諸偽將搒掠取其貲，大氐降者十七，刑者十三。

translations.literal: For lesser officials some were employed and some not: those employed were sent to the puppet government's personnel office for assignment; those not employed had their wealth beaten and plundered by the false generals—roughly seven in ten submitted, three in ten were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Junior officials were used or not as the case might be: those used were sent to the rebel government's board for appointment; those not used were beaten and robbed by the false generals. Roughly seven parts submitted and three were punished.

sentences.zh: 福王時，以六等罪治諸從逆者。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, six grades of crime were applied to those who had followed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu, six degrees of guilt were fixed for those who had joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 而文武臣殉難並予贈蔭祭葬，且建旌忠祠於都城焉。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials who had died for the cause were alike granted posthumous titles, hereditary honors, sacrifices, and burial—and a Shrine of Loyal Martyrs was built in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials who had died for the dynasty were alike granted posthumous titles, hereditary honors, state sacrifices, and burial, and a Shrine of Loyal Martyrs was raised in the capital.

sentences.zh: 曰正祀文臣，祀景文以下二十人，及大同巡撫衛景瑗、宣府巡撫朱之馮、布衣湯文瓊、諸生許琰四人。

translations.literal: For principal civil sacrifice were enshrined twenty men from Fan Jingwen onward, plus Grand Coordinator Wei Jingyuan of Datong, Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhifeng of Xuanfu, the commoner Tang Wenqiong, and the student Xu Yan—four more.
translations.idiomatic: Principal civil worship: Fan Jingwen and twenty others, with Grand Coordinator Wei Jingyuan of Datong, Grand Coordinator Zhu Zhifeng of Xuanfu, the commoner Tang Wenqiong, and the student Xu Yan—four in addition.

sentences.zh: 曰正祀武臣，祀新樂侯劉文炳、惠安伯張慶臻、襄城伯李國楨、駙馬都尉鞏永固、左都督劉文耀、山西總兵官周遇吉、遼東總兵官吳襄七人。

translations.literal: For principal military sacrifice were enshrined seven: the Marquis of Xinle Liu Wenbing, the Earl of Huian Zhang Qingzhen, the Earl of Xiangcheng Li Guozhen, the Commandant-escort Gong Yonggu, the Left Chief Commander Liu Wenyao, the general-in-chief of Shanxi Zhou Yuji, and the general-in-chief of Liaodong Wu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Principal military worship: the Marquis of Xinle Liu Wenbing, the Earl of Huian Zhang Qingzhen, the Earl of Xiangcheng Li Guozhen, the Commandant-escort Gong Yonggu, the Left Chief Commander Liu Wenyao, the Shanxi commander-in-chief Zhou Yuji, and the Liaodong commander-in-chief Wu Xiang—seven men.

sentences.zh: 曰正祀內臣，祀太監王承恩一人。

translations.literal: For principal eunuch sacrifice was enshrined the director Wang Chengen alone.
translations.idiomatic: Principal eunuch worship: the director Wang Chengen alone.

sentences.zh: 曰正祀婦人，祀烈婦成德母張氏，金鉉母章氏，汪偉妻耿氏，劉理順妻萬氏、妾李氏，馬世奇妾朱氏、李氏，陳良謨妾時氏，吳襄妻祖氏九人。

translations.literal: For principal female sacrifice were enshrined nine chaste martyrs: Zhang, mother of Chengde; Zhang, mother of Jin Xuan; Geng, wife of Wang Wei; Wan, wife of Liu Lishun, and Li, his concubine; Zhu and Li, concubines of Ma Shiqi; Shi, concubine of Chen Liangmo; and Zu, wife of Wu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Principal worship of women: nine martyred wives and mothers—Zhang, mother of Chengde; Zhang, mother of Jin Xuan; Geng, wife of Wang Wei; Wan, wife of Liu Lishun, and Li, his concubine; Zhu and Li, concubines of Ma Shiqi; Shi, concubine of Chen Liangmo; and Zu, wife of Wu Xiang.

sentences.zh: 曰附祀文臣，祀進士孟章明及郎中徐有聲，給事中顧鋐、彭琯，御史俞志虞，總督徐標，副使朱廷煥七人。

translations.literal: For ancillary civil sacrifice were enshrined seven: the jinshi Meng Zhangming and the director Xu Yousheng, the supervising secretaries Gu Yu and Peng Guan, the censor Yu Zhiyu, the grand coordinator Xu Biao, and the vice commissioner Zhu Tinghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ancillary civil worship: the jinshi Meng Zhangming; the director Xu Yousheng; the supervising secretaries Gu Yu and Peng Guan; the censor Yu Zhiyu; Grand Coordinator Xu Biao; and Vice Commissioner Zhu Tinghuan—seven men.

sentences.zh: 曰附祀武臣，祀成國公朱純臣、鎮遠侯顧肇跡、定遠侯鄧文明、武定侯郭培民、陽武侯薛濂、永康侯徐錫登、西寧侯宋裕德、懷寧侯孫維藩、彰武伯楊崇猷、宣城伯衛時春、清平伯吳遵周、新建伯王先通、安鄉伯張光燦、右都督方履泰、錦衣衛千戶李國祿十五人。

translations.literal: For ancillary military sacrifice were enshrined fifteen: the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Chunchen, the Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Zhaoji, the Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenming, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Peimin, the Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lian, the Marquis of Yongkang Xu Xideng, the Marquis of Xining Song Yude, the Marquis of Huaining Sun Weifan, the Earl of Zhangwu Yang Chongyou, the Earl of Xuancheng Wei Shichun, the Earl of Qingping Wu Zunzhou, the Earl of Xinjian Wang Xiantong, the Earl of Anxiang Zhang Guangcan, the Right Chief Commander Fang Lütai, and the Brocade Guard commander of a thousand Li Guolu.
translations.idiomatic: Ancillary military worship: fifteen men including the Duke of Chengguo Zhu Chunchen, the Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Zhaoji, the Marquis of Dingyuan Deng Wenming, the Marquis of Wuding Guo Peimin, the Marquis of Yangwu Xue Lian, the Marquis of Yongkang Xu Xideng, the Marquis of Xining Song Yude, the Marquis of Huaining Sun Weifan, the Earl of Zhangwu Yang Chongyou, the Earl of Xuancheng Wei Shichun, the Earl of Qingping Wu Zunzhou, the Earl of Xinjian Wang Xiantong, the Earl of Anxiang Zhang Guangcan, the Right Chief Commander Fang Lütai, and the thousand-commander of the Brocade Guard Li Guolu.

sentences.zh: 曰附祀內臣，祀太監李鳳翔、王之心、高時明、褚憲章、方正化、張國元六人。

translations.literal: For ancillary eunuch sacrifice were enshrined six directors: Li Fengxiang, Wang Zhixin, Gao Shiming, Chu Xianzhang, Fang Zhenghua, and Zhang Guoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ancillary eunuch worship: six directors—Li Fengxiang, Wang Zhixin, Gao Shiming, Chu Xianzhang, Fang Zhenghua, and Zhang Guoyuan.

sentences.zh: 有司春秋致祭。

translations.literal: The local officials performed seasonal sacrifices in spring and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates offered sacrifice each spring and autumn.

sentences.zh: 然顧鋐、彭琯、俞志虞輩，特為賊拷死，諸侯伯亦大半以兵死。

translations.literal: Yet Gu Yu, Peng Guan, Yu Zhiyu and the like had been killed only under rebel torture; most of the marquises and earls had also died by force of arms.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gu Yu, Peng Guan, Yu Zhiyu, and others had died only under rebel torture, and most of the marquises and earls had likewise perished in battle.

sentences.zh: 而郎中周之茂、員外郎寧承烈、中書宋天顯、署丞於騰雲、兵馬指揮姚成、知州馬象乾皆以不屈死，顧未邀贈恤也。

translations.literal: The director Zhou Zhimao, the vice director Ning Chengielie, the secretariat drafter Song Tianxian, the acting registrar Yu Tengyun, the horse-command director Yao Cheng, and the prefect Ma Xiangqian all died refusing to yield—yet they had not received posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: The director Zhou Zhimao, the vice director Ning Chengielie, the secretariat drafter Song Tianxian, the acting registrar Yu Tengyun, the horse-command director Yao Cheng, and the prefect Ma Xiangqian all died without submitting—yet none had been granted posthumous rewards.

sentences.zh: 徐有聲，字聞復，金壇人。

translations.literal: Xu Yousheng, courtesy name Wenfu, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yousheng, styled Wenfu, came from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 登鄉薦，崇禎十三年特擢戶部主事，歷員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination; in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he was specially promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and rose through vice director to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination; in the thirteenth year of Chongzhen he was specially promoted to principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to vice director and then director.

sentences.zh: 督餉大同。

translations.literal: He supervised grain transport at Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He was charged with supervising grain funds at Datong.

sentences.zh: 城陷，被執不屈死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was seized and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was taken and died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈太仆少卿。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 徐標，字準明，濟寧人。

translations.literal: Xu Biao, courtesy name Zhunming, was a native of Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Biao, styled Zhunming, came from Jining.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，歷官淮徐道參議。

translations.literal: Under Chongzhen he served in succession as junior commissioner for the Huai-Xu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he served in turn as junior commissioner on the Huai-Xu circuit.

sentences.zh: 十六年二月，超擢右僉都御史，巡撫保定。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixteenth year he was abruptly promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixteenth year he was suddenly promoted to Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 陛見，請重邊防，擇守令，用車戰禦敵，招流民墾荒。

translations.literal: On audience with the throne he asked to strengthen border defense, choose capable magistrates, use chariot warfare against the enemy, and recruit displaced people to reclaim wasteland.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he urged stronger frontier defense, the selection of able magistrates, chariot tactics against the enemy, and the settlement of refugees on abandoned land.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷山西，警日逼，加標兵部侍郎，總督畿南、山東、河北軍務，仍兼巡撫，移駐真定以遏賊。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Shanxi and alarms drew nearer by the day, Biao was made Vice Minister of War and given overall command of military affairs in southern Zhili, Shandong, and Hebei, still retaining his post as grand coordinator; he moved his headquarters to Zhending to block the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng seized Shanxi and danger closed in daily, Biao was made Vice Minister of War and given overall command of troops in southern Zhili, Shandong, and Hebei while remaining grand coordinator of Baoding; he shifted his headquarters to Zhending to hold the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 無何，賊遣使諭降，標毀檄戮其使。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels sent envoys urging surrender; Biao tore up the letter and executed their messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels sent envoys to demand his surrender; Biao tore up the letter and killed the messenger.

sentences.zh: 賊別將掠畿輔，真定知府邱茂華移妻孥出城，標執茂華下之獄。

translations.literal: A rebel detachment raided the capital region; the Zhending prefect Qiu Maohua moved his wife and children out of the city; Biao had Maohua arrested and thrown in prison.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel column raided the capital region; the Zhending prefect Qiu Maohua sent his wife and children out of the city; Biao had him arrested and jailed.

sentences.zh: 中軍謝加福伺標登城畫守禦策，鼓眾殺之，出茂華於獄。

translations.literal: The central army officer Xie Jiafu waited until Biao went up on the wall to draw up defense plans, then roused the men, killed him, and released Maohua from prison.
translations.idiomatic: His central-army officer Xie Jiafu waited until Biao went up on the walls to plan the defense, then incited the troops, killed him, and freed Maohua from prison.

sentences.zh: 數日而賊至，以城降。

translations.literal: Within days the rebels arrived and the city surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Within days the rebels came and the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈標兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the time of the Prince of Fu, Biao was posthumously made Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 朱廷煥，單縣人。

translations.literal: Zhu Tinghuan was a native of Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tinghuan came from Shan County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the seventh year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 除工部主事，歷知廬州、大名二府，即以兵備副使分巡大名。

translations.literal: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and in succession governed Luzhou and Daming prefectures, then was made vice commissioner for circuit defense with a separate commission over Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works, then in turn served as prefect of Luzhou and Daming, and was made vice commissioner for military preparedness with separate charge of the Daming circuit.

sentences.zh: 十七年，賊逼畿輔，廷煥嚴守備。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, as rebels pressed the capital region, Tinghuan strengthened the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, as rebels closed on the capital region, Tinghuan tightened the defenses.

sentences.zh: 賊傳檄入城，怒而碎之。

translations.literal: The rebels sent in a summons to the city; in anger he smashed it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent in a surrender summons; he tore it to pieces in fury.

sentences.zh: 三月四日，賊來攻，軍民皆走，城遂陷。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the third month the rebels came to attack; soldiers and civilians alike fled, and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the third month the rebels attacked; troops and people alike fled, and the city was lost.

sentences.zh: 被執不屈死。

translations.literal: Seized, he died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Taken captive, he died refusing to submit.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈右副都御史。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was posthumously appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 周之茂，字松如，黃麻人。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhimao, styled Songru, was a man of Huangma.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhimao, whose courtesy name was Songru, came from Huangma.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the seventh year of the Chongzhen reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官工部郎中。

translations.literal: He served in office as a director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 服闋，需次都下。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he awaited appointment in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period he waited in the capital for an appointment.

sentences.zh: 賊搜得之，迫使跪，不屈，折其臂而死。

translations.literal: The bandits searched him out, forced him to kneel; he would not submit, and they broke his arms until he died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels found him, forced him to kneel, and when he refused they broke both his arms and killed him.

sentences.zh: 寧承烈，字養純，大興人。

translations.literal: Ning Chengle, styled Yangchun, was a man of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Chengle, whose courtesy name was Yangchun, came from Daxing.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，歷魏縣教諭，戶部司務，進本部員外郎，管太倉銀庫。

translations.literal: He qualified in the provincial examination, served as instructor in Wei County and clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, was promoted to director in the ministry, and managed the silver vault of the Great Granary.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations, served as county instructor in Wei and as a clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, then was promoted to director in the ministry in charge of the Great Granary silver vault.

sentences.zh: 城陷，自經於官廨。

translations.literal: When the city fell he hanged himself in his government office.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he hanged himself in his yamen.

sentences.zh: 宋天顯，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Song Tianxian was a man of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Song Tianxian came from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 由國子生官內閣中書舍人。

translations.literal: Through the National University he became a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From a student of the Imperial Academy he was appointed secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為賊所獲，自經。

translations.literal: Seized by the bandits, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Captured by the rebels, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 於騰雲，順天人。

translations.literal: Yu Tengyun was a man of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Tengyun came from Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 為光祿置丞。

translations.literal: He served as assistant director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He held the post of assistant director in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 賊至，語其妻曰：「我朝臣，汝亦命婦，可汙賊耶！」

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived he said to his wife: "I am a minister of our dynasty; you are a noble wife as well—can you be defiled by bandits?
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came he told his wife, "I am a minister of this dynasty and you are a lady of rank—how can we be defiled by rebels?

sentences.zh: 夫婦並服命服，從容投繯死。

translations.literal: Husband and wife both put on their robes of office and calmly hanged themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Husband and wife donned their official robes and calmly hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 姚成，字孝威，余姚人。

translations.literal: Yao Cheng, styled Xiaowei, was a man of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Cheng, whose courtesy name was Xiaowei, came from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 由禮部儒士為北城兵馬司副指揮。

translations.literal: From a Confucian licentiate in the Ministry of Rites he became vice commander of the Northern City Horse and Infantry Patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a Confucian licentiate in the Ministry of Rites, he was made vice commander of the Northern City Horse and Infantry Patrol.

sentences.zh: 城陷，自縊死。

translations.literal: When the city fell he hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 馬象乾，京師人。

translations.literal: Ma Xiangqian was a man of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xiangqian was a native of the capital.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，官濮州知州。

translations.literal: He qualified in the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examinations and served as magistrate of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 方里居，賊入，率妻及子女五人並自縊。

translations.literal: While living in his home district the bandits entered; he led his wife and five children to hang themselves together.
translations.idiomatic: While at home in his native place the rebels entered; he led his wife and five children to hang themselves together.

sentences.zh: 至若御史馮垣登、兵部員外郎鄭逢蘭、行人謝於宣皆拷死，郎中李逢甲，拷掠久之，逼令縊死。

translations.literal: As for Censor Feng Yuandeng, Bureau of War Director Zheng Fenglan, and Messenger Xie Yuxuan—all were tortured to death; Director Li Fengjia was tortured for a long time and then forced to hang himself.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Feng Yuandeng, Bureau of War Director Zheng Fenglan, and Messenger Xie Yuxuan were all tortured to death; Director Li Fengjia was tortured at length and then compelled to hang himself.

sentences.zh: 與鋐、琯、志虞皆獲贈太仆少卿，而垣登、於宣至謚忠節。

translations.literal: Together with Jin, Guan, and Zhiyu they all received posthumous appointment as Vice Directors of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Feng Yuandeng and Xie Yuxuan even received the posthumous title Zhongjie.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Jin, Guan, and Zhiyu they were all posthumously made Vice Directors of the Court of the Imperial Stud; Feng Yuandeng and Xie Yuxuan were even granted the posthumous title Zhongjie.

sentences.zh: 行取知縣鄒逢吉拷死，贈太仆寺丞。

translations.literal: Promoted-from-magistrate Zou Fengji was tortured to death and posthumously made Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Fengji, a magistrate promoted to the capital, was tortured to death and posthumously appointed Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 時南北阻絕，皆未能核實也。

translations.literal: At the time north and south were cut off and none of these could be verified.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the north and south were severed from each other, and none of these cases could be confirmed.

sentences.zh: 湯文瓊、許琰事載《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: The affairs of Tang Wenqiong and Xu Yan are recorded in the "Account of Loyalty and Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The careers of Tang Wenqiong and Xu Yan are recorded in the Account of Loyalty and Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《傳》雲「君子居其位，則思死其官」。

translations.literal: The comment says: "The Classic says, 'When the gentleman occupies his post, he thinks of dying for his office.'"
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: "The Classic says, 'When a gentleman holds office, he is ready to die for it.'"

sentences.zh: 夫忠貞之士，臨危授命，豈矯厲一時，邀名身後哉！

translations.literal: Loyal and steadfast men who face peril and offer their lives—how could they be posturing for a moment to chase fame after death!
translations.idiomatic: Men of loyalty and integrity who meet danger and give their lives—how could they be striking poses for a moment to win posthumous renown!

sentences.zh: 分誼所在，確然有以自持而不亂也。

translations.literal: Where the bond of duty lies, they have something solid by which to hold themselves and not be thrown into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Where duty divides them, they have something firm to hold to and are not thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 馬世奇等皆負貞亮之操，勵志植節，不欺其素，故能從容蹈義，如出一轍，可謂得其所安者矣。

translations.literal: Ma Shiqi and the others all bore an unyielding integrity, strove to plant their moral standards, and did not betray their plain character; therefore they could calmly follow righteousness as one pattern—it may be said they found where they belonged.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiqi and the rest all possessed steadfast integrity, cultivated their principles, and did not betray their true nature; thus they could meet death for righteousness with the same composure—it may be said they died as they had lived.
